functions.name: find_programmer
functions.description: Print the first executable STM32CubeProgrammer CLI found from the explicit override, PATH or known installation locations; return 1 when no candidate is available. Takes no positional arguments. Checks override executability before PATH and bundle candidates; it prints only the chosen path on stdout and does not launch the programmer or inspect a connected board.

functions.name: find_loader
functions.description: Print the first existing board external-loader file found from the explicit override or installation paths beside the programmer supplied as argument 1; return 1 if none exists. Uses LOADER_NAME/STM32_EXTERNAL_LOADER overrides and checks file presence, not compatibility with a fitted QSPI device. stdout is consumed by the caller's command substitution.

functions.name: configure_embedded_library
functions.description: Apply CPU and section-splitting flags to an existing library named by target_name. Also mark assembly for C preprocessing. A nonexistent target is ignored; no value is returned, no sources are added and no global compiler flags are changed by this helper. Reusing one helper keeps the linked archives consistent with the executable's CPU ABI.

functions.name: lcd_error
functions.description: Enter the application Error_Handler, which disables interrupts and loops indefinitely. No arguments or return result; centralize the fatal path for display setup and address- switch failures. Error_Handler has no recovery path in this application, so callers do not receive an error status.

functions.name: lcd_panel_prepare
functions.description: Enable the LCD control GPIO clocks and configure output pins; hold backlight, display enable and reset low and select the display mode. Use board BSP GPIO macros, output push-pull/no-pull/low-speed, before applying the initial control levels. Assumes display-enable and backlight pins share the port used for their combined initialization. No GPIO HAL return status is checked.

functions.name: lcd_panel_power_on
functions.description: Assert LCD display enable, wait 20 ms, release reset and wait 120 ms using HAL delays. This ordered sequence controls the configured enable/reset pins, not the backlight. Delays are blocking HAL millisecond waits; their compatibility with the fitted panel remains a board-profile verification item.

functions.name: lcd_backlight_on
functions.description: Assert the LCD backlight GPIO after display setup. Drive the configured backlight control pin high after registration and cleared framebuffer setup. There is no brightness/PWM setting, failure return or later automatic shutdown.

functions.name: lcd_ltdc_msp_init
functions.description: Configure PLL3 for LTDC, enable LTDC/GPIO clocks, select the display alternate-function pins and reset LTDC; enter the error handler if the peripheral-clock configuration fails. No arguments; configure PLL3 M=5,N=160,R=83 and LTDC source, then AF14 RGB/control pins on K/I/J/H. HAL peripheral-clock failure enters the fatal path, while GPIO operations have no checked result. Reset/release LTDC after pin configuration; no fitted-panel identity is read.

functions.name: lcd_ltdc_init
functions.description: Initialize LTDC timing and its RGB565 layer at the first framebuffer address; enter the error handler on HAL initialization or layer configuration failure. Use BSP RK043FN48H constants, active-low sync/DE and input pixel-clock polarity; configure one opaque RGB565 layer at LCD_LAYER_0_ADDRESS sized LCD_DEFAULT_WIDTH by LCD_DEFAULT_HEIGHT. The horizontal HBP-minus-11 adjustment is retained: active timing calculates 491 clocks while the image layer is 480 pixels. This requires exact-panel evidence before alteration and is not exercised by host rendering.

functions.name: disp_flush
functions.description: LVGL flush callback: ignore area, clean/invalidate the data cache, point LTDC layer zero at color_p and signal completion through drv; enter the error handler if changing the address fails. LVGL supplies drv and the full-frame draw buffer color_p. Because full_refresh is enabled, area is intentionally unused and no pixel copy is made: flush all data cache then switch the LTDC layer base. Signal lv_disp_flush_ready immediately after HAL success; no explicit vertical-blank synchronization or controller-completion wait is present here.

functions.name: LCD_init
functions.description: Initialize SDRAM, LCD panel and LTDC, clear two full-screen framebuffers and register a full-refresh LVGL display before enabling backlight; duplicate initialization or failed hardware/display setup enters the error handler. Must follow lv_init and precede ui_init. Initialize BSP SDRAM instance zero, prepare controls/clocks/reset/timing, then zero two width*height buffers, maintain cache and register both as a full-screen LVGL draw buffer. display is a persistent registration pointer; a second call is fatal. Backlight is enabled only after nonnull registration. The host simulator uses a different memory display and does not run this routine.

functions.name: touchpad_read
functions.description: LVGL pointer callback: ignore drv, read the BSP touch state and fill data with pressed coordinates or the last position with released state; BSP read status is not checked. LVGL supplies writable data; no null guard is present. TouchX/TouchY are pixel coordinates after BSP orientation; save the last detected pair and reuse it on release so release events keep a position. Ignoring BSP_TS_GetState failure means the existing ts_state may be used after a failed read; no error/unknown event is synthesized.

functions.name: touchpad_init
functions.description: Initialize the BSP touch controller for LCD dimensions with XY swap and register an LVGL pointer read callback; return immediately if BSP initialization fails. No arguments or return status; select BSP instance zero, LCD pixel dimensions, TS_SWAP_XY and accuracy 5. BSP init failure silently leaves touch unregistered. Otherwise initialize the persistent LVGL driver and store the registration pointer without checking for null; repeated calls have no duplicate-registration guard.

functions.name: app_can_signal_is_fresh
functions.description: Check per-signal received validity and unsigned millisecond age.

functions.name: app_can_signal_name
functions.description: Provide names for diagnostics without assigning new vehicle protocol fields.

functions.name: app_can_log_init_failure
functions.description: Report the failing initialization stage when debug output is enabled and return false. stage names the failed setup operation. The return is always false so initialization callers can propagate failure directly; printing also reads the handle error code. It does not reset hardware or clear previously decoded data.

functions.name: app_can_abs_int32
functions.description: Return an absolute value for the signed int16-range values passed by the debug formatter. The result is a signed 32-bit magnitude used only for decimal formatting. Callers widen int16_t first, including -32768; the helper itself does not guard a general INT32_MIN input and has no state changes.

functions.name: app_can_clamp_int64_to_int16
functions.description: Saturate a wide signed result to the dashboard signed 16-bit storage range. Accept a signed 64-bit arithmetic result and return INT16_MIN/INT16_MAX at the limits, otherwise cast exactly. This bounds stored current means and power values without changing any accumulator.

functions.name: app_can_print_unsigned_deci_volts
functions.description: Print a labeled decivolt value with one decimal digit; ignore a null label. One input count means 0.1 V. Integer quotient and remainder produce a decimal V suffix without floating point; output has a leading space and no trailing newline. The snapshot is unchanged.

functions.name: app_can_print_unsigned_100uv_volts
functions.description: Print a labeled cell-voltage value in 100-microvolt units with four decimal digits. One input count means 0.0001 V. Divide by 10000 and zero-pad the remainder to four digits; a null label produces no output. This is formatting only and does not validate the measured range.

functions.name: app_can_print_signed_deci_amps
functions.description: Print signed deciamps as a labeled amperage with one decimal digit. One input count means 0.1 A. Widen before taking magnitude, preserve the sign separately, and print whole/fractional parts with A; null label returns before output. No statistics or sample fields change.

functions.name: app_can_get_display_voltage_deci_volts
functions.description: Prefer nonzero pack voltage, otherwise summed pack voltage; return zero for null data. The pointer is a retained CAN snapshot; return units remain 0.1 V. Zero is treated as a fallback trigger rather than as validity metadata. Neither source has an age check, and this function writes no state.

functions.name: app_can_compute_power_kw
functions.description: Convert deciamps times decivolts to integer kW, rounding half values away from zero. Both inputs are integer-scaled samples: current in 0.1 A and voltage in 0.1 V. A 64-bit product avoids intermediate overflow; division by 100000 converts to kW and the returned int16_t saturates if needed. This computes instantaneous power, not integrated energy.

functions.name: app_can_print_signed_integer
functions.description: Print a labeled signed integer when a label is supplied. value is printed in signed decimal without a units suffix or newline. The debug caller supplies the meaning through label; null label is a no-op and all measurement/statistics state remains unchanged.

functions.name: app_can_debug_log_request
functions.description: Log a PID submitted for transmission only when CAN debug output is enabled. pid is the 16-bit identifier just accepted by the HAL TX queue, printed in hexadecimal. This message does not establish delivery or a CAN acknowledgement; no pending-request fields are changed here.

functions.name: app_can_debug_log_timeout
functions.description: Log an outstanding PID that exceeded its timeout when CAN debug output is enabled. pid is the scheduler identifier whose elapsed request age exceeded the configured timeout. This helper only emits text; the polling caller clears pending state and advances the sequence.

functions.name: app_can_debug_log_response
functions.description: Log a validated eight-byte reply and its decoded measurement/statistics when debug is enabled. rx_data must address eight already-validated bytes and data must point to the post- decode snapshot. Select the matching PID field, add current/power statistics for current replies, and print fault_flags. Null pointers or disabled debugging produce no output; neither input is mutated.

functions.name: app_can_enable_gpio_clock
functions.description: Enable one supported GPIO A-I peripheral clock, returning false for another port. port is a HAL GPIO register pointer. The A through I pointer comparisons select exactly one RCC clock-enable macro; success means a supported port was selected, not a pin or transceiver test. No HAL error result is available from these macros.

functions.name: app_can_set_debug_enabled
functions.description: Enable or disable CAN initialization, request, response and timeout serial diagnostics. enabled replaces the module-wide boolean consulted by initialization, TX, RX and timeout printers. It has no return value and does not stop CAN requests or protect against concurrent console output.

functions.name: app_can_is_debug_enabled
functions.description: Return the current CAN diagnostic-output setting. Return the module-wide debug boolean without side effects. DEBUG builds start with true, other builds false; later calls to the setter override that default.

functions.name: app_can_config_is_supported
functions.description: Accept only a nonnull configuration selecting the implemented classic CAN mode. Only mode is examined after the null guard: APP_CAN_MODE_FD is declared in the interface but not implemented here. Instance validity, pins and electrical compatibility are not checked by this predicate.

functions.name: app_can_clamp_percentage
functions.description: Limit a decoded unsigned state-of-charge percentage to 100. value is an unsigned integer percent after the SOC decoder conversion. Values 0 through 100 pass through; larger values return 100. It neither reports invalid raw data nor attaches a validity flag.

functions.name: app_can_decode_orion_current_deci_amps
functions.description: Subtract the implemented 32767 raw-current offset and saturate to signed deciamps. The existing protocol interprets the big-endian raw 16-bit word as an offset-binary number with zero at 32767. Return units are 0.1 A; raw 65535 would produce 32768 and is therefore clipped to 32767. This is the implemented encoding, not confirmation of a future BMS protocol.

functions.name: app_can_update_current_stats
functions.description: Accumulate accepted current samples into signed min/max and nearest-integer mean values. data must contain the newly decoded current in 0.1 A. The first sample seeds persistent min/max/sum/count; subsequent samples update them and write rounded signed mean/min/max back into the snapshot. Every accepted current reply counts, including duplicates; there is no time window, session reset or count-overflow handling in this helper.

functions.name: app_can_update_power_stats
functions.description: Accumulate integer-kW min/max/mean at current-sample time when voltage is fresh. Use fresh pack voltage, or fresh summed voltage, with the newly decoded current. Round each power sample to integer kW before maintaining persistent min/max/sum/count and writing the rounded mean. Null data or absent/stale voltage leave statistics unchanged. Sampling has no freshness pairing or time integration.

functions.name: app_can_get_next_request_pid
functions.description: Return the PID at the current position in the ten-request round-robin table. The private index must remain in the request-table range. Return the table PID without advancing it or changing pending state; initialization and the advance helper establish that invariant.

functions.name: app_can_advance_request_sequence
functions.description: Advance the ten-request round-robin position and wrap from the final PID to the first. Increment the private request enum modulo APP_CAN_REQUEST_COUNT. The polling caller invokes this only on timeout or a reply matching the pending PID; sending a request does not advance it.

functions.name: app_can_dlc_to_bytes
functions.description: Translate a HAL DLC constant to its payload-byte count; unknown constants map to zero. data_length_code uses HAL-encoded DLC constants, not a byte count. Mapping includes legal FD lengths up to 64 so the receiver can reject them after HAL has copied into the 64-byte scratch buffer. This conversion does not itself accept a frame.

functions.name: app_can_send_pid_request
functions.description: Submit one padded classic eight-byte service-0x22 request when initialized and TX space exists. pid becomes big-endian bytes 2 and 3 after PCI 0x03 and service 0x22; remaining bytes are zero padding. TX uses standard ID 0x7E3, eight-byte classic data format and no BRS. Return false before enqueue if uninitialized or FIFO full, or after a HAL enqueue failure. Success only enqueues; polling records pending PID/time afterward.

functions.name: app_can_response_length_is_valid
functions.description: Accept only the table's exact ISO-TP single-frame length; larger PCI values include other frame types. pid selects a table entry and pci_length is the complete first payload byte. Equality with 4 or 5 enforces the implemented single-frame form and excludes multi-frame PCI values. Unknown PID returns false; no data or scheduler state changes.

functions.name: app_can_decode_orion_response
functions.description: Validate standard classic data-frame metadata and exact single-frame length, then decode a known PID. Require nonnull pointers, standard classic data ID 0x7EB, exactly eight payload bytes, service 0x62 and the known PID-specific PCI. Reconstruct 16-bit values big-endian; summed voltage rounds raw hundredths of volts into decivolts, current subtracts 32767, SOC halves/rounds/clamps, temperatures cast to signed Celsius, and cell values retain 100-microvolt units. A valid current reply also mutates module statistics. Other failures return false without updating the supplied snapshot. Matching a pending request is not required; fault_flags is not decoded.

functions.name: app_can_handle_rx_message
functions.description: Publish a successfully validated reply to the latest dashboard snapshot and optionally log it. Start from a copy of the retained snapshot so fields outside this PID survive. A successful decoder call publishes the whole updated copy and prints it; false leaves the retained snapshot untouched. It does not compare the reply PID to pending state; polling performs that separate sequence operation.

functions.name: app_can_init
functions.description: Initialize FDCAN using the board configuration and response-ID filter; report failures for caller retry. With no arguments, return true immediately if already initialized. Select HSE, normal classic mode and automatic retransmission; allocate one exact-ID standard filter, eight RX FIFO0 slots and one TX FIFO slot. Clock/init/filter/start failures return false for task retry. Only full success marks ready and resets request position/pending/time; existing measurement/statistics storage is not cleared. At the configured 25 MHz HSE, prescaler 5 with 1+8+1 time quanta calculates 500 kbit/s.

functions.name: app_can_poll_dashboard_data
functions.description: Expire overdue requests, drain valid replies, and send the next PID every 50 ms when idle. Always copy the retained snapshot on initialized polls; unsigned elapsed-time arithmetic supports tick rollover. data is caller storage for a full snapshot. Return true only after an accepted reply. Capture HAL milliseconds once; expire pending requests only when unsigned elapsed time is strictly greater than 100 ms, then drain FIFO0 until empty or HAL read failure. Valid unsolicited/duplicate replies still update measurements, while only a matching PID clears pending and advances. When idle and elapsed time is at least 50 ms, enqueue the next request and record its time on success. Return false for null/uninitialized input or no accepted reply; consumers evaluate per-signal age.

functions.name: HAL_FDCAN_MspInit
functions.description: Configure clocks and RX/TX alternate-function pins only for the configured FDCAN instance. The HAL callback handle must match the immutable configured instance. Unsupported/null inputs return silently; supported port clocks are enabled before AF push-pull, no-pull, very-high-speed RX and TX pins are configured independently. FDCAN1 additionally enables its RCC clock. This function does not configure bus timing or test physical routing.

functions.name: HAL_FDCAN_MspDeInit
functions.description: Release RX/TX pins and the FDCAN1 clock only when the handle matches the board configuration. For a matching nonnull handle/configuration, deinitialize both configured GPIO pins, then disable the clock for FDCAN1. Other handles return without changes. It does not clear app_can_initialized or retained measurements and is a HAL resource callback, not the application shutdown API.

functions.name: app_can_config_get
functions.description: Return the immutable FDCAN instance, pins and classic-CAN mode used by the application. The returned pointer references static const storage with program lifetime: FDCAN1, GPIOH RX14/TX13, AF9, classic mode. Callers must not modify it; there is no allocation, runtime configuration or failure branch.

functions.name: app_ui_abs_int32
functions.description: Return the magnitude of value for current-to-display conversion; the callers pass int16_t current values, so INT32_MIN is outside their input range. Return a signed 32-bit magnitude with no state changes. Widening int16_t before the call preserves its most-negative value; no generic INT32_MIN guard exists.

functions.name: app_ui_slider_from_temperature
functions.description: Convert signed Celsius to the UI slider range 1 through 100 by clamping; return the display value without changing the sample. Input units are signed whole degrees Celsius. Negative, zero and very cold samples all display at the minimum, and samples above 100 display at the maximum; this display clamp does not diagnose temperature faults.

functions.name: app_ui_text
functions.description: Format text into an LVGL label when the label exists. Screens are optional here: missing objects (for example after a SquareLine re-export without the runtime screens) are skipped instead of reaching LVGL's NULL assertion.

functions.name: app_ui_set_voltage_mv_label
functions.description: If label exists, convert voltage from 100-microvolt units to rounded millivolts and replace its LVGL text; null labels are ignored. Input units are 100 microvolts per count; adding five before division by ten rounds to millivolts. The decimal label contains no units suffix. Only the LVGL object text changes; the integer sample is preserved.

functions.name: app_ui_set_signed_integer_label
functions.description: Replace an existing LVGL label with the signed decimal value; ignore a null label. The caller determines units (currently integer kW statistics); this helper formats signed base-ten text and has no range conversion. Only an existing object is touched and null is a no-op.

functions.name: app_ui_calculate_usage_percent
functions.description: Return used/total as a rounded integer percentage, or zero for zero capacity; the 64-bit intermediate arithmetic prevents multiplication overflow. used and total must use the same units (records or bytes). Add half of total for nearest-integer rounding before division; return is not clamped at 100 if used exceeds total. The helper does not read logger state itself.

functions.name: app_ui_get_status_panel
functions.description: Return the LVGL panel pointer mapped to signal_id, or NULL for the count sentinel or an unknown signal; do not create objects. The seven switch arms preserve the generated screen variable names, including ui_panleReadyToDrive. The returned object is borrowed from ui_init and must not be freed here; the mapping has no side effects.

functions.name: app_ui_get_status_label
functions.description: Return the LVGL label pointer mapped to signal_id, or NULL for the count sentinel or an unknown signal; do not create objects. Use the same enum order as status_signals and map each entry to its generated LVGL label. Objects are borrowed and may still be null before screen creation; invalid enum values return null.

functions.name: app_ui_set_object_hidden
functions.description: Set or clear the LVGL hidden flag according to hidden; ignore a null object. hidden changes only LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN on the borrowed object; color and text remain unchanged. A null pointer is safe, and this function allocates no objects.

functions.name: app_ui_set_status_indicator_color
functions.description: Apply color to the selected signal panel border and label text when those objects exist. signal_id selects both objects and color is an LVGL color value, not a raw hex integer. Set border/text color for LV_PART_MAIN and default state; absent panel and label are checked separately.

functions.name: app_ui_drive_mode_to_text
functions.description: Return the static N, D or R label for a drive mode, or a dash for an unknown mode. drive_mode is the internal enum, with COUNT only a sentinel. Return a borrowed string literal requiring no allocation or freeing; no CAN message or physical selector is interpreted.

functions.name: app_ui_update_aux_placeholders
functions.description: Update state from elapsed milliseconds using synthetic speed and drive-mode cycles; after the boot interval mark status inputs initialized and leave every digital fault inactive. No CAN or GPIO input is read; null state is ignored. now_ms is elapsed milliseconds; unsigned differences drive one speed increment of 3 km/h per qualifying call at 200 ms intervals, bouncing at 0 and 160. Missed intervals are not replayed. Persistent static state is shared across calls; N/D/R advances every 5000 ms after first initialization. At 3000 ms status_inputs_initialized becomes true; all seven statuses are always set valid and nonfaulted. This automatic firmware demo has no reset API and is bypassed by explicit host inputs.

functions.name: app_ui_apply_aux_state
functions.description: Apply auxiliary values to existing objects, rendering unknown speed/mode as dashes. Unknown digital inputs use neutral colors; show every status during boot or when any input is unknown or faulted, and hide them only when all inputs are known healthy. Ignore null state. state is read-only input, now_ms controls the 3000 ms boot display. Speed uses integer km/h and mode uses the internal enum; absent validity produces dashes and gray mode styling. Status visibility is group-wide: show all seven during boot/uninitialized input or if any status is unknown/faulted; otherwise hide all seven. Within a visible group each indicator is gray for unknown, red for valid fault, green for valid healthy. This changes LVGL objects only and does not read or invert GPIO.

functions.name: ui_fresh
functions.description: Test validity independently for each measurement; zero is a valid received value.

functions.name: ui_gauge_valid
functions.description: Hide an unknown gauge's fill and mask; leave the existing outline visible.

functions.name: ui_signal_state
functions.description: LIVE for fresh, STALE for received-then-old, MISSING for never received.

functions.name: app_ui_apply_at
functions.description: Render values with explicit age, leaving layout independent of data. The cell table keeps the SquareLine rows: cell voltage, temperature, the "Battery kWh" row (since-boot power statistics in kW, as originally bound) and SPEED (filled by app_ui_refresh). Pack voltage, summed voltage, current and SOC go to the pack screen; logger and CAN counters to the history status line.

functions.name: app_ui_apply_dashboard_data
functions.description: Compatibility binding uses LVGL time; production paths use explicit shared clock below.

functions.name: app_ui_apply_speed_statistics
functions.description: Fill the SquareLine SPEED row with since-boot maximum, mean and minimum km/h of valid samples. Unwired or currently unknown speed shows "--"; no speed is ever invented.

functions.name: app_ui_refresh
functions.description: Render live state and record malfunction episodes, never clearing previous events.

functions.name: app_data_log_get_oldest_index
functions.description: Return zero until the RAM ring is full, then return the next write position as the oldest sample index; callers read this state inside a critical section. The private head is the next write slot. Before saturation samples begin at physical slot zero; at full count the next write slot is also the oldest retained slot. No array copy occurs and the helper itself does not enter a critical section.

functions.name: app_data_log_init
functions.description: Initialize the RAM sample ring by resetting all samples and counters. No inputs or return value; delegate to reset and discard any current RAM history. This initializes only the RAM ring, not CAN statistics or eMMC sessions.

functions.name: app_data_log_reset
functions.description: Clear the RAM ring, write index, count and wrapped flag while interrupts are protected by the FreeRTOS critical section. Zero the complete fixed-capacity state, including sample storage, head, count and wrap flag. It does not clear persistent eMMC or synchronize an ongoing multi-row CSV dump as one transaction.

functions.name: app_data_log_record
functions.description: Copy timestamp_ms and data into the RAM ring inside a critical section, replacing the oldest sample once full and setting the wrap flag; ignore null data. timestamp_ms is a caller-provided uint32_t millisecond value and is stored without ordering checks. Copy the full snapshot by value, advance head modulo 4096 and cap count at 4096. wrapped becomes true on the first overwrite after filling, not on the write that initially reaches capacity. Recording does not apply measurement validation or persistent storage.

functions.name: app_data_log_get_capacity
functions.description: Return the compile-time capacity of the RAM sample ring; no state is changed. Return 4096 records, independent of current occupancy. No lock is needed because this is a compile-time constant and no storage is read or mutated.

functions.name: app_data_log_get_count
functions.description: Return a critical-section-protected snapshot of the retained RAM sample count. The return is the number of currently retained records, 0 through 4096, not total lifetime writes. The critical section covers only the counter read; separately requested status values are not one combined transaction.

functions.name: app_data_log_is_wrapped
functions.description: Return a critical-section-protected snapshot indicating that a write has replaced an existing sample. Return the sticky boolean set after overwriting a full ring and cleared by reset. It describes lost oldest RAM history, not eMMC overflow or a CAN error.

functions.name: app_data_log_get_sample
functions.description: Copy the retained sample at index_from_oldest into sample inside a critical section; return false for a null output or an index outside the current count, otherwise true. index_from_oldest is a zero-based logical index; convert to physical array position modulo 4096 and copy both timestamp and dashboard fields. The output remains untouched on false. Bounds/index/copy share one critical section, but successive calls can observe different ring generations.

functions.name: app_data_log_dump_csv
functions.description: Print a CSV header and the retained RAM samples in oldest-first index order. Each sample is copied separately, so concurrent recording can change the ring while the dump runs. Take count once, then fetch rows one by one with get_sample. Printed fields keep their integer storage units and signedness; failures skip rows. printf is outside per-sample critical sections, so acquisition can continue and a full-ring dump is not a coherent frozen snapshot.

functions.name: app_diag_label
functions.description: Create plain bounded text in the existing diagnostic font/color system.

functions.name: app_diag_grid
functions.description: Draw the debug table's red grid at the same 10..470 x 12..258 coordinates as the SquareLine DebugFrame image: a 38 px header and four 52 px rows. An empty middle header merges the two value columns.

functions.name: app_diag_navigate
functions.description: Load another existing screen; the history page is brought up to date first.

functions.name: app_diag_long_press_main
functions.description: Same gesture and transition as the SquareLine debug screen: long press returns to main.

functions.name: app_diag_page
functions.description: Move one page toward newer (user data non-NULL) or older events, clamped at both ends.

functions.name: app_diag_button
functions.description: Add a bordered text button in a table cell or the history footer.

functions.name: app_diag_screen
functions.description: Make a black fixed-size root that returns to main on long press.

functions.name: app_diagnostics_ui_init
functions.description: Create the extra screens once; measurement text is filled by the runtime binding.

functions.name: app_diag_show_journal
functions.description: Describe where new events go; anything but SAVED is shown in a warning color.

functions.name: app_diag_show_event
functions.description: Fill one history row from a copied event; returns false when the slot could not be read.

functions.name: app_diagnostics_ui_refresh_history
functions.description: Render four newest-first copied events; storage is read only when the page changed.

functions.name: app_diagnostics_ui_screen_name
functions.description: Name the active root for host commands, tests and the live simulator.

functions.name: app_diagnostics_ui_destroy
functions.description: Delete the extra roots and their owned labels; history itself is independent of screens.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_lock
functions.description: Take the logger mutex with an indefinite FreeRTOS wait; return false if the mutex has not been created or the take fails. There are no arguments; successful return means the caller owns the single module mutex. portMAX_DELAY can block the calling task without a finite timeout. Helpers ending _locked rely on this ownership rather than taking the mutex again.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_unlock
functions.description: Release the logger mutex if it exists; ignore the FreeRTOS give result. This balances a successful lock or already-held helper chain. There is no return value or owner validation in this wrapper; it does not flush records or alter logger readiness.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_crc32_update
functions.description: Update a caller-supplied, unfinalized reflected CRC-32 accumulator with size bytes using polynomial 0xEDB88320; return the unchanged accumulator for null data. crc is the previous raw accumulator, size is bytes, and data must expose that many bytes. XOR each byte into the low bits and perform eight reflected polynomial shifts. Do not initialize or complement here; callers choose whether this is a whole-buffer or concatenated-stream calculation.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_crc32_compute
functions.description: Return a CRC-32 computed from size bytes with all-one initialization and final XOR, using the logger CRC update routine. Use seed 0xFFFFFFFF and complement the returned update accumulator to create the finalized CRC. The underlying updater returns its seed for null data, so this wrapper returns zero for null data rather than an error code.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_record_crc32
functions.description: Return the CRC-32 of the in-memory record bytes before its crc32 member, including any structure padding; return zero for null record. The record is the native storage structure, not the 42-byte portable wire record. offsetof excludes the stored checksum field; padding before that field participates in the checksum. Callers zero-initialize records before populating fields; padding still participates in the checksum.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_record_crc_is_valid
functions.description: Compare the stored record CRC with a recalculated CRC over the preceding bytes; return false for a null record. record points to a copied native storage record. The result is an integrity comparison only; it neither repairs corrupted content nor checks measurement ranges or header/session validity.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_write_le16
functions.description: Write value into the caller-provided two-byte buffer in little-endian order; the buffer must be valid. buffer must expose at least two writable bytes; shifts/masks explicitly encode low byte first independent of host structure layout. No bounds/null check or state beyond those two bytes is provided.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_write_le32
functions.description: Write value into the caller-provided four-byte buffer in little-endian order; the buffer must be valid. buffer must expose at least four writable bytes; each byte is extracted explicitly in increasing significance. No allocation, bounds/null check or external I/O occurs.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_uart_write_bytes
functions.description: Transmit size bytes synchronously on COM1 with HAL_MAX_DELAY; return false for null/empty data or a HAL UART failure, otherwise true. size is a uint16_t byte count and data must remain valid during the synchronous send. Success means HAL_UART_Transmit returned HAL_OK, not that a receiver validated the payload. The indefinite HAL timeout can hold an export and its logger mutex.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_build_header
functions.description: Populate the supplied storage header from current session counters, configured region and overflow state after clearing it; ignore a null header. header must be writable storage for the 512-byte header. Fill magic/version, region/session identity, native record size, counts, active/overflow flags and latest millisecond timestamp; unused bytes become zero. This builds metadata in RAM and adds no header CRC or persistence itself.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_write_header_locked
functions.description: Write the current session header to the reserved eMMC start block and return the BSP write result as a boolean; the caller must hold the logger mutex. Write exactly one 512-byte block at absolute logical block 4096 using BSP instance zero. Successful write clears header_dirty; failure leaves it available for retry. Header counters describe current RAM state, including accepted staged records, and no power- loss transaction is implemented.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_flush_locked
functions.description: While the caller holds the mutex, persist dirty staged records and the session header. Keep a partial tail in RAM so later records rewrite its remaining slots, counting its physical block once. Release a full tail; retry a failed header even with no dirty data. Return false if unready, out of reserved blocks or a write fails. The 512-byte data block is padded with 0xFF beyond block_fill. A new tail is written at start+1+written_blocks; an already-written partial tail reuses the prior address. Increment physical block count only on its first write, retain partial contents for later append, and release the buffer when another native record cannot fit. On data- write failure leave dirty state for retry; on header failure the data may already be persisted. Overflow marks metadata and attempts its header write before returning false.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_start_new_session_locked
functions.description: Replace the current session identifier and clear record/block counters, staged bytes and overflow, then write the new eMMC header; return the write result. The caller must hold the mutex. next_session_id is used exactly as supplied, including unsigned rollover. Discard staged data and logical history by resetting counters and flags; existing data blocks are not erased. Header write failure returns false after RAM state has already changed; callers update readiness accordingly.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_get_records_per_block
functions.description: Return how many in-memory records fit in one eMMC block, or zero when record size is zero. Integer division truncates the unused padding at the end of each 512-byte block. Consumers use this quotient to map logical record index to block and slot, avoiding interpretation of padding as records. The size is sizeof the native record, not portable export size.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_pack_dump_record
functions.description: Serialize a record into the caller-provided dump buffer in little-endian field order, including stored-CRC validity, stored CRC and a new dump CRC; return bytes written, or zero for null input/output. buffer must have 42 writable bytes; encode timestamp, scaled dashboard fields, integrity flag, stored native CRC and finalized portable CRC. Signed 16-bit values preserve their bit pattern through uint16_t conversion and signed temperatures occupy one byte. The portable layout contains no native padding. stored_crc_valid is reported as supplied and does not prevent serialization of corrupted storage content.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_init
functions.description: Create/take the logger mutex, initialize the eMMC BSP and size the reserved region to the card. Read the prior header only to choose the next session ID, then start a new session; return readiness and release the mutex on all locked paths. No prior-session records are resumed. Cap the requested 262144-block region against reported LogBlockNbr after requiring space beyond start+one header; recognize only magic/version in a readable old header for next session ID. Allocation, lock, BSP init/card-info/capacity or new-header failure produces false. Successful init sets readiness and a new empty session; it does not prove reserved-region ownership or physical card identity.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_append
functions.description: Stage a timestamped copy of data with its storage CRC under the mutex, flushing a block when necessary and advancing session counters; return false for invalid/unready input or lock/flush failure. Success can leave the record staged in RAM. timestamp_ms is copied as milliseconds without monotonicity checks and data is copied by value. A zero-initialized native record gets a CRC before staging; acceptance increments logical count immediately. If a later automatic flush fails, false can follow staging/count mutation. A normal true result can mean RAM-only staging; durability requires flush. Null data, oversized record, unready logger, locking, reserved-space or flushing errors return false.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_flush
functions.description: Take the mutex, flush staged eMMC records and release the mutex; return false if locking or flushing fails, otherwise true. This public wrapper does not require caller mutex ownership. The locked helper can rewrite a partial data tail or only retry dirty metadata; no staged data and clean header succeed when ready. The returned boolean does not report how many records/bytes were persisted.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_reset_session
functions.description: Under the mutex, increment the session ID, discard staged records and reset counters by writing a new header; update readiness and return the header write result. No arguments; use unsigned session_id+1 and replace logical history with a new empty session. The reset does not erase all reserved blocks or preserve staged records. Lock failure returns false without reset, while header failure has already cleared session state and marks readiness false.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_get_status
functions.description: Clear and populate the caller status structure with a mutex-protected logger snapshot; ignore null status and leave zeros if locking fails. status is caller writable storage. Clear it first so a missing/failed mutex leaves an all-zero snapshot; on success copy readiness/overflow/session/count/block fields atomically under the mutex. staged_bytes counts only an unallocated tail: a retained already-written tail contributes zero even after another append, avoiding double-counted allocated storage.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_dump_csv
functions.description: Hold the logger mutex, flush staged records, read stored blocks and print each sample with its stored-CRC validity. Return without output when setup fails and stop rows at a block read failure. Logical records are mapped using records-per-block and cached one block at a time. Validate native CRC and print the boolean even for invalid records; integer fields keep storage units. Read failure yields a truncated CSV with no boolean return. The mutex remains held through flushing, reads and printf, preventing concurrent append/status operations.

functions.name: app_emmc_log_dump_binary
functions.description: Hold the logger mutex and flush staged data, then transmit the HFDB header, packed records and HFDE footer on COM1 with header/record/stream/footer CRCs; return false on lock, storage, packing or UART failure, otherwise true. Emit a 24-byte HFDB header, record_count portable 42-byte rows and a 16-byte HFDE footer, all little-endian. Header CRC covers its first 20 bytes; row CRC covers first 38; stream CRC covers complete rows using one raw accumulator then final XOR; footer CRC covers first 12. Stored native-CRC validity is a row flag and does not abort export. Any error may leave a partial stream without footer, so the receiver must validate count and all checksums. The mutex stays held through synchronous UART output.

functions.name: app_emmc_fault_capacity
functions.description: Report reserved fault slots after card discovery, clamped to the card; never overlaps telemetry.

functions.name: app_emmc_fault_decode
functions.description: Decode a portable 28-byte checksummed event inside a dedicated 512-byte slot.

functions.name: app_emmc_fault_read
functions.description: Read a fault slot under the telemetry mutex; I/O failure is reported apart from corruption.

functions.name: app_emmc_fault_wait_ready
functions.description: Wait until the card is transfer-ready; bounded polling prevents a permanent GUI stall.

functions.name: app_emmc_fault_write
functions.description: Append without altering occupied bytes; verify a full-slot write before acknowledging it.

functions.name: app_fault_history_init
functions.description: Initialize a boot's observation state without offering a way to delete records.

functions.name: app_fault_event_shape_valid
functions.description: Reject records whose checksum passed but whose fields this firmware cannot interpret.

functions.name: app_fault_history_attach
functions.description: Find the end of the written prefix by binary search, then check the last record. Appends are strictly sequential, so slots before the end are occupied and slots after it are erased; boot cost is O(log capacity) reads instead of one read per stored event. A corrupt final slot is a torn last write and is skipped, never rewritten. Any other inconsistency blocks new writes so the evidence stays as found. An I/O error leaves the journal detached for this boot; events are then kept in RAM.

functions.name: app_fault_history_flush
functions.description: Flush queued immutable records, leaving failed and later events intact for retry.

functions.name: app_fault_history_observe
functions.description: Record state/detail transitions once, with copied immutable values and boot-relative time.

functions.name: app_fault_history_get
functions.description: Copy by index; callers can never edit the journal through a returned pointer.

functions.name: app_fault_history_count
functions.description: Return immutable history length.

functions.name: app_fault_history_dropped
functions.description: Report capacity loss explicitly.

functions.name: app_fault_history_pending
functions.description: Report events that are still volatile.

functions.name: app_fault_history_journal_state
functions.description: Explain persistence in priority order; full journals cannot promise future retention.

functions.name: app_fault_history_durable
functions.description: Report persistence availability.

functions.name: app_fault_history_session
functions.description: Return this boot's ID after journal recovery has advanced it past saved boots.

functions.name: app_fault_source_name
functions.description: Name diagnostics without inventing vehicle wiring or CAN fields.

functions.name: app_fault_monitor_set_limits
functions.description: Copy caller limits so later edits to the caller's table cannot change detection.

functions.name: episode_bad
functions.description: Record a bad state when it starts or changes kind; repeats of the same kind add nothing.

functions.name: episode_good
functions.description: Record CLEAR once the condition has stayed healthy for hold_ms; no entry if none is open.

functions.name: counter_update
functions.description: Open an episode once increments have been seen for confirm_ms while counting, extend it on later increments and close it after APP_FAULT_ERROR_QUIET_MS without any. ACTIVE detail is the running total when confirmed; CLEAR detail is the number of counted increments. Increments while counting is false (timeouts during a link outage, which the BMS link episode already records) are absorbed: not counted, and they cancel an unconfirmed start.

functions.name: signal_value
functions.description: Return one received measurement in its native units for limit comparison.

functions.name: signal_age
functions.description: Age of a received signal on the GUI clock; a sample stamped after now counts as fresh.

functions.name: check_can
functions.description: BMS link first, then per-signal episodes only while the link is up. A whole-link outage is one entry, not ten. A signal is individually missing when its siblings keep updating but it has not (or never has) for APP_CAN_STALE_MS after the link came up.

functions.name: check_input
functions.description: Wired inputs only: fault is recorded at once, missing data after the startup grace.

functions.name: check_storage
functions.description: Card availability, write failures (state or counted between refreshes) and telemetry space.

functions.name: app_fault_monitor_update
functions.description: Evaluate every source for one GUI refresh.

functions.name: describe_value
functions.description: Format a CAN measurement in display units for limit entries.

functions.name: app_fault_describe
functions.description: Explain an event in words; unknown combinations fall back to raw state and detail.

functions.name: app_console_print_help
functions.description: Print the supported single-character UART console commands to the configured printf output. No inputs or return value; one printf lists the implemented character-to-command mapping. It neither executes those operations nor guarantees exclusive UART ownership.

functions.name: app_console_print_log_info
functions.description: Read RAM log counters and print count, capacity and wrap status to the console. No inputs; call independent protected getters and format decimal counts plus a 0/1 wrap flag. Acquisition can occur between getter calls, so this is informational output rather than a transaction snapshot.

functions.name: app_console_print_emmc_log_info
functions.description: Read the eMMC logger status snapshot and print readiness, session, record/block counts and overflow state. Get one mutex-protected status structure then print the ready/overflow booleans and session/block/record counts. The block denominator includes the reserved metadata block; printing occurs after the status lock is released.

functions.name: app_console_handle_command
functions.description: Dispatch one UART command to log inspection, dump, clear/reset/flush or CAN debug control. Binary/CSV eMMC dumps temporarily suppress CAN debug output and restore it afterward; unknown commands print help. command is a single received byte; upper/lowercase letters share actions, CR/LF do nothing. RAM dumps/clear, eMMC info/flush/reset/CSV/binary and diagnostic toggle have their switch-defined side effects. CSV/binary temporarily change the global CAN debug setting but provide no global UART output lock. Binary return status is deliberately ignored; flush/reset commands print their boolean result.

functions.name: app_fault_dump_step
functions.description: Print a few history events per GUI pass as CSV, oldest first, so a long history neither stalls the display nor races the history owner. next is the following index, or UINT32_MAX when no dump is in progress.

functions.name: app_gui_task
functions.description: FreeRTOS entry point with an unused argument: initialize LVGL, LCD, touch and screens, then consume the latest CAN snapshot, refresh live diagnostics and service LVGL on the configured 5 ms schedule; never return. argument is unused. The task alone owns normal LVGL calls: initialize library/display/touch/generated objects before any binding, drain the queue without waiting, refresh measurements/malfunction episodes every 100 ms and stream a requested history dump a few rows per pass. LVGL time advances by measured HAL elapsed time, including storage delays; services timers, then delays against last_wake. Queue overwrites can omit intermediate UI states; LCD fatal errors halt, touch initialization can silently return.

functions.name: app_can_rx_task
functions.description: FreeRTOS entry point with an unused argument: retry CAN initialization, poll received dashboard updates, timestamp and record each update in RAM/eMMC, and overwrite the one- element UI queue; delay between polls and never return. argument is unused. Retry initialization at 1000 ms on failure; after readiness poll every 10 ms. One true poll can aggregate several accepted responses into one latest snapshot, recorded with the FreeRTOS tick-derived millisecond timestamp in RAM and eMMC before queue overwrite. eMMC append and queue results are ignored, so task output does not establish persistent success. CAN priority is one level above GUI/console.

functions.name: app_console_task
functions.description: FreeRTOS entry point with an unused argument: print initial log/help status, receive single bytes from COM1 and execute console commands; echo non-binary-dump commands, delay between reads and never return. argument is unused. HAL_UART_Receive reads one byte with a 50 ms timeout, and only HAL_OK dispatches. Echo printable ASCII normally, but omit echo for b/B to keep the binary header first; UART failures/timeouts are ignored before the 5 ms task delay. Dumps execute synchronously inside this task and can delay future commands.

functions.name: app_tasks_start
functions.description: Initialize the loggers, allocate the one-element dashboard queue and create GUI, CAN and console tasks; return false on queue/task allocation failure, otherwise true. eMMC initialization failure does not stop task creation. Call before starting the scheduler. RAM initialization is unconditional and eMMC failure is ignored; allocate a queue holding exactly one full snapshot, then GUI/CAN/console tasks in that order. Stack sizes are FreeRTOS words (2048/1024/1024), not bytes. False returns on the first allocation failure without deleting resources/tasks already created. The function starts neither the scheduler nor a physical input binding.

functions.name: main
functions.description: Start firmware from the reset handler; there are no caller arguments and successful execution stays inside the FreeRTOS scheduler. Configure MPU regions before enabling instruction/data caches, then initialize HAL, clocks and the COM1 debug console. Initialize QSPI in QPI/DTR dual-flash mode and enable memory mapping before any UI code or assets placed at 0x90000000 can be used. Barriers and instruction-cache invalidation follow the mapping change. Print the build/debug settings, wait 50 ms, create application tasks and start scheduling. A QSPI error, task-creation failure or scheduler return enters the nonreturning Error_Handler. This path is not executed by the desktop synthetic runner; mapped flash must be programmed separately on hardware.

functions.name: SystemClock_Config
functions.description: Configure the board power and clock tree; takes no parameters and returns only after the checked HAL configuration calls succeed. Select LDO supply, request voltage scale 1 and poll VOSRDY. Unsigned HAL-tick subtraction gives a wrap-tolerant timeout test strictly greater than 100 ms. A supply failure or readiness timeout halts in Error_Handler. Enable HSE and PLL1 with M=5, N=160, P=2, Q=4 and R=2; disable HSI/CSI. With the configured HSE_VALUE of 25 MHz, the requested PLLP/system rate is 400 MHz, HCLK 200 MHz and divided APB clocks 100 MHz. These are configuration calculations, not measured frequencies. HAL oscillator/clock failures halt; the final flash latency is four wait states.

functions.name: Error_Handler
functions.description: Terminate normal application progress after a fatal initialization/runtime error. No input, status code or recovery is provided. Disable maskable interrupts and execute NOP forever. This preserves a halted state for debugger inspection but does not save fault registers, export logs, reset the MCU or define a physical safe-output policy. Callers cannot continue after this function.

functions.name: vApplicationStackOverflowHook
functions.description: FreeRTOS callback for a detected task-stack overflow. xTask and pcTaskName identify the affected task, but this implementation deliberately discards both. Enter Error_Handler, disabling maskable interrupts and halting permanently. The hook does not print the task name or recover memory; its invocation depends on the configured kernel stack- check mechanism.

functions.name: DebugConsole_Init
functions.description: Configure BSP COM1 for diagnostic printf output: 115200 baud, eight data bits, one stop bit, no parity and no hardware flow control. Zero-initialize the local configuration, initialize the BSP port and select it as the BSP log destination. Both BSP return codes are checked and failures enter Error_Handler. This mutates UART/BSP state; it neither configures the binary log-export protocol nor validates a connected serial device.

functions.name: MPU_Config
functions.description: Establish memory-access/cache attributes before caches and application peripherals are enabled. No arguments or return status are exposed. Disable the MPU, reuse one zero-initialized descriptor and configure four numbered full- access, executable, nonshareable, cacheable, nonbufferable regions: AXI SRAM 0x24000000/512 KiB; D2 SRAM 0x30000000/256 KiB; SDRAM 0xD0000000/32 MiB; QSPI 0x90000000/128 MiB. Enable the privileged default map afterward. The attributes describe CPU access policy rather than physical capacity. The supplied BDP exposes 8 MiB of SDRAM, so the 32 MiB MPU region is a documented bounds-reconciliation gap; this function does not test memory or initialize its controllers.

functions.name: Reset_Handler
functions.description: Reset entry selected by the vector table; takes no C arguments and never returns normally. Load the main stack pointer from linker symbol _estack, then call SystemInit before RAM globals are initialized. Copy word-aligned initialized data from _sidata in flash to the half-open SRAM range [_sdata, _edata); clear [_sbss, _ebss) with zero words. Those bounds come from the linker script, not from hard-coded allocation sizes in this routine. Run __libc_init_array for static initialization, then call main. A main return branches forever. There is no memory-controller probe, bounds validation or error report here; this startup is excluded from the desktop runner and requires a correct firmware image.

functions.name: Default_Handler
functions.description: Fallback exception/interrupt entry for weak vector aliases without a linked override. Branch indefinitely to retain the stopped context; no C parameters, status code, device acknowledgment, diagnostic capture or recovery are supplied. Board/kernel handlers with matching strong symbols replace these aliases at link time; the vector table itself does not establish that every named peripheral interrupt is enabled or implemented.

functions.description: Initializes the Global MSP. / /** Global MCU-support hook invoked by HAL initialization. Enable the SYSCFG peripheral clock and return; no arguments or error status are used. This active function does not initialize CAN, UART, LTDC or DMA pins. Those resources are configured by the application/BSP routines; the numerous peripheral examples retained below this hook are line-commented and do not execute.

No arguments, diagnostic capture or recovery are provided; the handler never returns to the interrupted context. Unlike Error_Handler, this body does not explicitly disable maskable interrupts.

The handler loops without reading fault-status registers or the stacked program counter and does not return a status or restart the task. The body is an infinite loop, with no address/status-register capture, recovery or caller-visible result. Its definition describes the exception response, not evidence that a particular MPU access failed.

functions.name: BusFault_Handler
functions.description: This function handles Pre-fetch fault, memory access fault. / /** Stop permanently for a bus-fault exception. The function takes no arguments and never returns; it does not identify the failing bus/address, change peripheral state or attempt to recover the interrupted instruction.

functions.name: UsageFault_Handler

Loop without recording the hardware fault flags, reporting a cause or resuming execution; the source does not implement a recovery policy.

The wrapper takes no C parameters and performs no application work before delegation. The port owns the exception-frame/register semantics and scheduler startup. This is a vector entry wrapper, not a normal task-level call to start or switch the application.

functions.name: DebugMon_Handler
functions.description: This function handles Debug monitor. / /** Return from the debug-monitor exception without application action. All user sections are empty; no debugger message, peripheral update, status return or fault-recovery mechanism is supplied.

functions.name: PendSV_Handler
functions.description: This function handles Pendable request for system service. / /** Route the pending-supervisor vector to xPortPendSVHandler. The FreeRTOS port owns context saving/restoring and task-switch decisions; this wrapper adds no state or validation and has no C arguments or result.

The scheduler-state guard prevents kernel tick handling during HAL/startup delays before scheduling begins. The source also forwards when the scheduler is suspended; the kernel decides the resulting bookkeeping. No synthetic runner tick is delivered through this hardware ISR.

functions.description: This function handles MDMA global interrupt. / /** Forward the MDMA interrupt to BSP_SDRAM_IRQHandler for instance zero. The BSP-owned handle determines transfer handling; this wrapper neither configures an MDMA transfer nor supplies a status result. Empty user sections have no runtime effect.

functions.name: initialise_monitor_handles
functions.description: Functions */ /** Provide the libc monitor-initialization symbol with an empty body. Takes no arguments, returns no value and opens no semihosting, debugger or filesystem handles. Presence of this stub allows linkage without supplying a host operating system.

functions.name: _getpid
functions.description: Return the fixed integer 1 as libc's process identifier. No real process table or task lookup occurs, and no state or errno is changed. The value is a stub contract, not a FreeRTOS task ID.

functions.name: _kill
functions.description: Reject libc process signaling for any pid and sig. Both integer inputs are ignored, errno is set to EINVAL and -1 is returned. No task is notified, stopped or removed.

functions.name: _exit
functions.description: Implement nonreturning libc termination for an integer status. Pass status as the pid argument to the unsupported _kill stub with signal -1, then loop forever. The function does not reset the MCU, stop FreeRTOS scheduling explicitly, flush logs or return to main. The resulting errno is incidental to the stub call, not an exit-status delivery mechanism.

functions.name: _read
functions.description: Weak libc byte-input hook: fill ptr with len calls to the weak __io_getchar hook and return len. file is ignored, so descriptor numbers do not choose an input stream. The caller must supply valid writable storage and a nonnegative length; this body does not validate either. Character-hook errors and partial reads are not handled, and the peripheral/blocking behavior depends on the linked hook implementation.

functions.name: _write
functions.description: Weak libc byte-output hook: send len bytes from ptr through __io_putchar and return len; file is ignored. This bridges libc output to the linked character hook rather than to an operating-system file. The body does not validate the buffer/length, propagate character-hook failures or report short writes. A strong board/BSP implementation can override this weak symbol; concurrent serialization is not supplied here.

functions.name: _close
functions.description: Report unsupported descriptor closing by ignoring file and returning -1. No descriptor/resource is released and errno is not assigned in this body, so callers cannot infer a particular error cause from it.

functions.name: _fstat
functions.description: Treat any file descriptor as a character device by assigning st->st_mode = S_IFCHR and returning zero. file is ignored; other struct stat fields remain as supplied by the caller. The stat pointer must be valid because no null check is made. This is a libc compatibility stub rather than discovery of a physical device or file size.

functions.name: _isatty
functions.description: Return 1 for every descriptor, ignoring file. This makes libc treat the supplied descriptor as terminal-like without checking a UART or descriptor table; no state or errno is changed.

functions.name: _lseek
functions.description: Ignore file, ptr offset and dir origin and return zero. No stored position or peripheral state changes. The zero return is a stub response and does not mean that actual file data was seekable.

functions.name: _open
functions.description: Reject every path/flags/optional-argument request with -1. path and flags are ignored, no varargs are read, no filesystem entry is accessed and errno is not set by this body. The implementation supplies linkage, not filesystem support.

functions.name: _wait
functions.description: Reject waiting for child processes: ignore the status pointer, set errno to ECHILD and return -1. No value is written through status and no FreeRTOS task is joined or blocked.

functions.name: _unlink
functions.description: Reject removal of a filesystem name. Ignore name, set errno to ENOENT and return -1; no path is dereferenced and no storage record or directory entry is removed.

functions.name: _times
functions.description: Return (clock_t)-1 for process-times queries and ignore buf. No fields of the caller's tms structure are filled and no HAL or kernel time is read; errno is not assigned here.

functions.name: _stat
functions.description: Pretend the supplied path identifies a character device: ignore file, set st->st_mode to S_IFCHR and return zero. All remaining stat fields are untouched. Requires a valid st pointer; no path lookup, null check or physical-device detection is implemented. This matches the minimal libc stub behavior, not a real filesystem query.

functions.name: _link

functions.name: starm_putc

This redirects the output to the low-level __io_putchar function. @param c Character to write. @param file FILE stream pointer (ignored). @retval int The character written. / /** Picolibc FILE-stream output callback, compiled only under __PICOLIBC__. functions.name: _sbrk
functions.description: _sbrk() allocates memory to the newlib heap and is used by malloc and others from the C library @verbatim ############################################################################ #  .data  #  .bss  #       newlib heap       #          MSP stack          # #         #        #                         # Reserved by _Min_Stack_Size # ############################################################################ ^-- RAM start      ^-- _end                             _estack, RAM end --^ @endverbatim This implementation starts allocating at the '_end' linker symbol The '_Min_Stack_Size' linker symbol reserves a memory for the MSP stack The implementation considers '_estack' linker symbol to be RAM end NOTE: If the MSP stack, at any point during execution, grows larger than the reserved size, please increase the '_Min_Stack_Size'. @param incr Memory size @return Pointer to allocated memory / /** Adjust the separate libc heap watermark by signed byte count incr and return the previous watermark. Initialize it lazily from linker symbol _end; positive requests grow the heap and negative requests move the watermark backward. Use _estack minus linker-reserved _Min_Stack_Size as the upper bound. If the requested end exceeds that limit, set errno to ENOMEM, return (void *)-1 and keep the watermark unchanged. This reserves space for the main stack; it does not detect actual stack depth. There is no lower-bound check for shrinking and no task synchronization or allocation-size validation here. This hook backs libc allocation and is distinct from FreeRTOS heap_4/configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE. Under Picolibc, sbrk is a strong alias of this same implementation.

Takes no arguments and supplies no error result. Enable FPU access when compiled for an FPU, restore RCC clock registers to the source's reset defaults, disable RCC interrupts and apply the revision-Y AXI workaround selected by DBGMCU IDCODE. Conditional DATA_IN_D2_SRAM enables those SRAM clocks; DATA_IN_ExtSDRAM invokes the early memory helper; VECT_TAB_SRAM chooses SRAM vector relocation, otherwise VTOR uses internal flash plus VECT_TAB_OFFSET. functions.name: SystemCoreClockUpdate
functions.description: Update SystemCoreClock variable according to Clock Register Values. The SystemCoreClock variable contains the core clock , it can be used by the user application to setup the SysTick timer or configure other parameters. @note   Each time the core clock changes, this function must be called to update SystemCoreClock variable value. Otherwise, any configuration based on this variable will be incorrect. @note   - The system frequency computed by this function is not the real frequency in the chip. It is calculated based on the predefined constant and the selected clock source: - If SYSCLK source is CSI, SystemCoreClock will contain the CSI_VALUE(*) - If SYSCLK source is HSI, SystemCoreClock will contain the HSI_VALUE(**) - If SYSCLK source is HSE, SystemCoreClock will contain the HSE_VALUE(***) - If SYSCLK source is PLL, SystemCoreClock will contain the CSI_VALUE(*), HSI_VALUE(**) or HSE_VALUE(***) multiplied/divided by the PLL factors. (*) CSI_VALUE is a constant defined in stm32h7xx_hal.h file (default value 4 MHz) but the real value may vary depending on the variations in voltage and temperature. (**) HSI_VALUE is a constant defined in stm32h7xx_hal.h file (default value 64 MHz) but the real value may vary depending on the variations in voltage and temperature. (***)HSE_VALUE is a constant defined in stm32h7xx_hal.h file (default value 25 MHz), user has to ensure that HSE_VALUE is same as the real frequency of the crystal used. Otherwise, this function may have wrong result. - The result of this function could be not correct when using fractional value for HSE crystal. @param  None @retval None / /** Refresh SystemCoreClock and SystemD2Clock in hertz from current RCC register selections; this function reads hardware and updates two software globals, not the clock tree itself. Choose HSI, CSI, HSE or PLL1; for PLL1 reconstruct the multiplier, optional fractional contribution, input divider and P divider. A zero PLL M divider yields zero rather than division by zero. Apply D1 core and AHB prescalers through D1CorePrescTable. Accuracy depends on HSI_VALUE/CSI_VALUE/HSE_VALUE matching their real sources. No external measurement or HAL error status is performed; callers must invoke an update after clock changes when their timing code uses these globals.

It exists so external memory can be accessible before C runtime data initialization, rather than as the normal LCD/BSP initialization path. Write fixed FMC alternate-function GPIO settings, SDRAM bank/timing registers, command sequence and refresh count directly; command busy waits use countdowns and the initial delay is a loop count rather than a calibrated millisecond delay. Enable the controller and discard the temporary RCC-read variable. No parameter selects a fitted memory part, and expiration of a command wait is not reported. These retained register constants must not be interpreted as a verified profile for every MB1381 revision; the current build does not enable the optional DATA_IN_ExtSDRAM define in this file.

functions.name: crc32_bytes
functions.description: Compute the unsigned standard CRC-32 used for binary dump framing. Input data is an immutable byte sequence. Return binascii.crc32(data) masked to 32 bits; do not mutate bytes or maintain incremental state. This is used for header, footer and per-dump-record checks, while read_dump carries its separate CRC across complete wire records.

functions.name: parse_args
functions.description: Parse export-source and output controls from process argv. Require exactly one of --port (UART device) and --input-bin (offline Path). Defaults: baud 115200 bits/s, output prefix emmc_dump and header wait 15 seconds. Return the argparse Namespace; argument errors terminate through argparse. This parser does not open either source or validate the binary contents.

functions.name: read_exact
functions.description: Read a required fixed-size byte region from a binary stream. Ser may be a file, BytesIO or serial-style object; size is bytes. Make one read call and return only if its length equals size. Otherwise raise RuntimeError with expected/actual lengths. Stream position advances; partial reads are not retried or accumulated here, and underlying read errors propagate.

functions.name: wait_for_header
functions.description: Find the UART binary-export header amid preceding incoming bytes. Ser is a binary stream with timeout-capable reads; timeout_s uses wall-clock seconds measured by monotonic. Read one byte at a time, retaining only the last four until HFDB appears, then read the remaining fixed header bytes via read_exact. Return the complete header; raise RuntimeError on deadline or short header. Consumes preceding text/noise and changes stream position; it sends no command.

functions.name: unpack_header
functions.description: Validate and decode one 24-byte little-endian HFDB stream header. Input bytes must match HEADER_STRUCT. Require magic HFDB, version 1, header size 24, record size 42 and CRC over all header bytes except its last CRC field. Return version/session_id/record_count/flags; sizes and CRC are validation metadata. Wrong fields/checksum raise RuntimeError, wrong byte length may raise struct.error. No records are read here, and caller-owned bytes remain unchanged.

functions.name: read_dump
functions.description: Read and validate an entire version-one binary export from its current position. Stream supplies binary bytes; optional raw_output receives each consumed header, record and footer verbatim. header_bytes may be the already-scanned UART header; otherwise read it now. Validate header first, read its declared number of 42-byte records, decode each row and incrementally CRC all complete wire records starting with binascii state zero. Read/validate the 16-byte HFDE footer and require its record count and stream CRC to match. Return (header, rows). Framing/short reads/count/stream-CRC failures raise RuntimeError; row-level stored and dump CRC validity are returned as flags rather than rejected here. This reader does not check bytes after the footer; the offline CLI does. Streams advance and raw_output may contain a partial capture if later validation fails.

functions.name: unpack_record
functions.description: Decode one 42-byte wire record without altering firmware integer units. Unpack little-endian fields into RECORD_FIELDS: milliseconds, decivolts/deciamps, 100-microvolt cell counts, integer kW, SOC, signed degrees C and flags/CRCs. Append dump_crc_valid from a CRC over all bytes except the final dump CRC, and stored_crc_valid from record_flags bit 0 (the firmware's stored-record result). Return the row even when either flag is false; malformed length raises struct.error. The Python reader does not independently recompute the stored C record's CRC.

functions.name: unpack_footer
functions.description: Validate and decode the 16-byte little-endian HFDE export footer. Input bytes must match FOOTER_STRUCT. Require HFDE and CRC over the twelve bytes before footer_crc. Return record_count and stream_crc; compare those with header and accumulated record bytes later in read_dump. Wrong magic/checksum raises RuntimeError and wrong length may raise struct.error. No stream/file mutation.

functions.name: write_csv
functions.description: Export decoded record rows with raw firmware units and CRC-validity columns. Path is the destination and rows the dictionaries returned by unpack_record. Replace/create a UTF-8 CSV, preserving RECORD_FIELDS column order, then append stored_crc_valid/dump_crc_valid. Write the header even for zero rows and return None. Directory/file/CSV errors propagate; engineering rescaling is not performed.

functions.name: write_xlsx
functions.description: Export the same raw-unit rows to an optional Excel workbook. If openpyxl was unavailable at import, return False without writing a file. Otherwise create eMMC Dump, append the ordered field/validity headers and each row, save to path and return True. Existing destination may be replaced; workbook or filesystem errors propagate. Rows are not changed or converted into new units.

functions.name: main
functions.description: Capture or decode a binary dump, then write raw/CSV/optional XLSX exports. Read CLI arguments and derive .bin/.csv/.xlsx paths from the prefix. Offline mode rejects input aliases (including hard links) to all outputs, reads/validates the stream while copying exact bytes, then rejects trailing bytes. UART mode requires pyserial, opens the configured device, resets buffers, waits 0.2 seconds, sends ASCII b and scans for HFDB before reading the export. This hardware path exists in this standalone utility but is not invoked by the synthetic runner/tests. Write tabular exports, print session/count/file locations and invalid stored/dump CRC row counts, then return 0. Row CRC flags are reported, not automatically fatal here. Argument/validation/serial/filesystem failures propagate; files written before a late failure can remain. No physical operation is required for --input-bin.
