functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_production_stream_crc_is_accepted_by_serial_cli.FakeSerial.__init__
functions.description: Start reads at the first captured firmware byte regardless of UART options. Accept arbitrary serial-constructor args/kwargs solely for interface compatibility. Initialize BytesIO with the enclosing production capture and return None; UART options do not select any device or alter the deterministic byte source.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_production_stream_crc_is_accepted_by_serial_cli.FakeSerial.reset_input_buffer
functions.description: Leave the deterministic capture intact when the CLI requests buffer reset. Return None without changing BytesIO position/content so the captured firmware header remains available. This emulates only the reset method required by exporter main and intentionally has no device buffer side effect.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_production_stream_crc_is_accepted_by_serial_cli.FakeSerial.reset_output_buffer
functions.description: Ignore output reset because commands are asserted rather than queued. Return None; no outbound queue exists in this fixture. The write method checks the only supported request directly, so buffer clearing must not change input bytes.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_production_stream_crc_is_accepted_by_serial_cli.FakeSerial.write
functions.description: Check the binary export request without replacing the capture contents. Input command must be exactly ASCII b. Return its byte count without replacing the BytesIO capture or advancing reads; raise AssertionError for any other command. This proves the CLI export request while performing no serial transmission.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_dump_then_append_crosses_block_boundary_once
functions.description: Repeated flush/dump followed by slots 12 and 13 must retain all thirteen records. Decode the C slots scenario after repeated dump/flush and append through slot 13. Require ordered timestamps 1..13 and every stored CRC flag valid. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_full_capacity_rejects_next_record_without_counting_it
functions.description: A one-data-block fake card must export its twelve records and overflow flag. Run a one-data-block fake card. Require header count 12, overflow flag 1 and exact timestamps 1..12; the rejected next sample must not affect exported count. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_unflushed_append_automatically_crosses_block_boundary
functions.description: A thirteen-sample burst without caller flushes must produce two contiguous blocks. Run the automatic thirteen-sample burst with no caller flushes. Require contiguous ordered timestamps 1..13 and valid stored flags across two blocks. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_reset_session_discards_old_tail_and_restarts_counters
functions.description: Explicit reset must release a retained tail and export only the new session sample. Run the explicit reset case. Require session ID 2 and only timestamp 99, showing old retained-tail data is not reused as a new-session record. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_status_does_not_double_count_retained_tail_allocation
functions.description: Usage counters must omit retained-tail bytes already covered by written_blocks. Run the C status scenario, which checks retained-tail usage counters, then require all thirteen exported timestamps remain ordered and intact. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_write_read_and_uart_failures_are_retryable
functions.description: Injected data/header/read/UART errors must not shift records or lose successful counts. Run the adapter errors mode, which injects data/header/read/UART failures. Require ordered timestamps 1..12 and valid stored CRCs after its retry sequence. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_empty_session_flush_is_repeatable
functions.description: An empty session must export a header/footer with zero records and zero stream CRC. Run the empty-session case. Require zero decoded records and footer stream CRC zero; header/footer framing is still validated. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_storage_corruption_is_reported_in_export_record_flag
functions.description: A damaged fake eMMC byte must survive export only with the stored CRC invalid flag. Run the fake-card corrupt case. Require the first stored CRC flag false but its newly produced dump CRC true, and the unaffected second stored flag true. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_reader_round_trips_all_signed_fields_and_raw_bytes
functions.description: The portable capture reader must preserve C units, signed extrema and exact wire bytes. Decode the C partial capture while copying raw output. Compare known raw units and signed extrema (-32768/32767 deciamps, -128 C) plus flags; copied bytes must match. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_wire_corruption_is_rejected_at_header_stream_and_footer
functions.description: Single-byte damage at each framing layer must be rejected by the actual capture reader. Flip one byte in the header, first record and final footer CRC independently. Require the reader to identify Header CRC, Stream CRC and Footer CRC failures. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_footer_count_mismatch_is_rejected_with_valid_crc
functions.description: A self-consistent footer CRC cannot excuse a count different from the header. Change footer record count to three and recompute its own CRC. Require the header/footer count comparison to fail despite internally consistent footer bytes. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_unsupported_version_and_truncated_capture_are_rejected
functions.description: Future versions and missing record/footer bytes must not be treated as valid captures. Set version 2 and recompute header CRC, then truncate a valid capture at several header/record/footer boundaries. Require version or exact-read errors respectively. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_offline_cli_works_without_serial_and_keeps_input
functions.description: A fake-eMMC capture must export to CSV without a UART library or device. Write a production partial capture, patch serial unavailable and run --input-bin. Require successful .bin/.csv export, unchanged source and raw decivolt field 4011. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: StorageExportTests.test_offline_cli_rejects_self_overwrite_and_trailing_data
functions.description: Reject input/output path aliases and malformed trailing bytes before claiming success. Provide an empty stream with trailing bytes. First require output-alias rejection and preserved source, then use a distinct prefix and require trailing-data rejection. Return None on success; unittest assertions or unexpected errors fail this case.

functions.name: _positive
functions.description: Parse a CLI numeric string into a finite positive float. The caller determines units: duration/request period are simulation seconds and rate is simulation seconds per wall-clock second. Reject zero/negative, overflow, NaN, infinity and malformed numbers as argparse.ArgumentTypeError. Return the float; parsing has no bus or filesystem effects.

functions.name: _log_frame
functions.description: Write a frame event as one flushed JSON line to stdout. Event labels the direction, elapsed is simulation seconds rounded to six decimal places, and message supplies arbitration ID, actual DLC/payload and frame flags. Return None after print; this records bytes already sent/received and does not send another frame. stdout write errors propagate.

functions.name: run
functions.description: Execute the virtual responder using a wall-clock-paced simulation timeline. Arguments select scenario, optional duration override, transport/channel, rate and optional demo request period. Open a responder endpoint and, for demo mode, a same-channel client in this process; ExitStack closes both on exit. Scale monotonic wall time by rate. Demo cycles the ten PID requests and skips missed periods instead of flooding catch-up requests. Step the responder, print TX/RX JSON events, drain at most 1024 demo replies per loop, and sleep briefly. Stop once simulation duration is reached, then print/return traffic summary including pending unsent frames. This CLI is paced rather than the deterministic millisecond C host runner. Configuration, transport and I/O errors propagate; pending delayed replies are not force-flushed after the stop time.

functions.name: main
functions.description: Parse CAN-simulator arguments and map execution failures to process exit codes. Read argv with argparse; defaults are virtual backend, rate 1 and demo request period 0.05 simulation seconds. --demo is required to originate built-in request traffic. Call run, returning 0 on success, 130 for KeyboardInterrupt, or 2 after printing validation/I/O/CAN/queue failures to stderr. Argument errors are handled by argparse. This entry point never permits a physical CAN backend.

functions.name: Responder.__init__
functions.description: Store a validated Scenario and initialize this responder's request-loss state. Input scenario provides tracks and fault intervals. Create a fresh counter dict keyed by fault index; the constructor emits no frames and returns None. Counters belong to this instance and advance only for active matching drop faults in plan.

functions.name: Responder.plan
functions.description: Plan response frames for a request at finite nonnegative simulation seconds. Ignore unrecognized request shapes by returning []. Select active faults, count matching drop requests and return [] for drop cadence or pause. Sample the engineering value at request time, so delayed delivery does not resample it. Combine raw override, additive delay, duplicate counts and burst counts; spacing is the largest active duplicate spacing. More than 4096 copies raises OverflowError. Encode once, mutate ID/service/PCI/PID before truncating to the smallest requested DLC, then deep-copy each scheduled response so copies have independent Message objects. Same-field mutations follow configuration order. Return due times in seconds and frames; validate finite times. No bus send occurs here; only drop counters mutate. Invalid elapsed/encoding raises ValueError.

functions.name: Runner.__init__
functions.description: Own the dispatch state for a supplied bus and response planner. Bus is an already-open python-can endpoint and responder plans frames without transmitting. max_pending is a positive non-bool integer frame limit (default 4096); invalid limits raise ValueError. Allocate a heap, stable tie-break sequence, clock initialized at zero and received/accepted/sent counters. Return None; bus lifetime remains the caller's responsibility.

functions.name: Runner.pending
functions.description: Report the number of queued responses not yet sent. Read the heap length and return a frame count. This includes both due and future responses, changes no queue/counter state, performs no bus access and does not include already transmitted frames awaiting reception at the other endpoint.

functions.name: Runner._send_due
functions.description: Transmit due heap entries in deterministic due-time/sequence order. Input elapsed is simulation seconds already validated by step. Pop at most 512 entries whose due <= elapsed, send each with a 0.05-second bus timeout, increment sent after successful send and return those Messages. Future entries stay queued. Bus errors propagate; an entry is popped before send, so failed transmission is not automatically requeued. No wall-clock scheduling is performed here.

functions.name: Runner.step
functions.description: Advance virtual response dispatch at one nondecreasing simulation timestamp. Require finite elapsed seconds >= the last clock (initially zero), otherwise raise ValueError. Send existing due entries, then receive up to 256 requests without waiting. Count all received frames and separately recognized requests; ask Responder for plans and reject queue growth beyond max_pending with OverflowError before inserting that request's plans. Stable sequence numbers order equal-time heap entries. Send newly due entries and return both sent lists. A step can send up to 512 frames in each of its two send phases. Clock, queue, planner counters and traffic counters mutate; transport errors propagate.

functions.name: finite_number
functions.description: Normalize a supplied number into the float used by scenario calculations. Input value is unitless here; label identifies the field in error messages. Accept int/float only, explicitly excluding bool despite its int subclass. Convert once and reject overflow, NaN and infinity with ValueError. Return the finite float; this helper performs no clamping, mutation or transport I/O.

functions.name: validate_value
functions.description: Validate a named battery value before constructing its CAN payload. Signal is a key of SIGNALS; value uses that key's engineering unit (V, A, percent or degrees C). Resolve the table entry, require a finite number, then enforce its inclusive minimum/maximum. Return the float unchanged in engineering units. Unknown names and invalid/range-exceeding values raise ValueError; no state changes.

functions.name: encode_response
functions.description: Construct a classic standard-CAN response for one implemented battery PID. Signal/value use SIGNALS engineering units. Validate value even when raw_override is supplied. Normally compute round-half-up(value * scale) + offset using Decimal, then mask to the payload width; masking represents signed temperature bytes. An explicit raw integer override must fit the width and allows deliberately unphysical wire extrema without accepting an invalid engineering input. Return a new eight-byte Message on 0x7EB: single-frame length, service 0x62, big-endian PID, one/two big-endian value bytes and zero padding. PCI length counts service, PID and value, excluding PCI/padding. Invalid values/overrides raise ValueError; message check validates framing. No bus send or shared state mutation.

functions.name: make_request
functions.description: Construct one read request matching the firmware request table. Input signal must name a SIGNALS entry. Return a fresh standard eight-byte 0x7E3 Message containing [3, 0x22, PID high, PID low, 0, 0, 0, 0]. The first byte describes the three service/PID bytes rather than the padded DLC. Unknown signals raise ValueError. This builds bytes only and does not transmit them.

functions.name: request_signal
functions.description: Classify an incoming frame as one of the ten supported read requests. Input is a python-can Message. Require ID 0x7E3, standard classic data framing, DLC 4..8 equal to actual data length, PCI 3 and service 0x22 before reading PID. Return the table's signal name for its big-endian PID; return None for every unrecognized ID/type/header/PID. The length checks precede indexing. The function neither changes the received message nor replies on a bus.

functions.name: _object
functions.description: Check the shape and allowed keys of one parsed JSON object. Input value is arbitrary JSON, allowed is the supported key set, and label gives error context. Return the original dict, without copying/mutating it, only if it contains no unknown fields. Otherwise raise ValueError. Required fields and value types are checked later by the caller, not by this shape-only helper.

functions.name: _integer
functions.description: Parse a bounded fault parameter, including explicit-base integer strings. Minimum/maximum are inclusive raw integer bounds; label appears in errors. For strings use int(value, 0), permitting forms such as 0x123. Reject booleans, floats (including integral-looking floats), unsupported strings and out-of-range numbers with ValueError. Return an int and perform no I/O or shared mutation.

functions.name: _unique_object
functions.description: Build a JSON object while preserving evidence of duplicate input keys. json.loads supplies ordered (key, value) pairs through object_pairs_hook at every object level. Create a new dict, raising ValueError immediately on a repeated key rather than letting the later value overwrite earlier configuration. Return that dict; no previously returned scenario object is modified.

functions.name: Track.value_at
functions.description: Sample this validated ordered track at elapsed simulation seconds. Use bisect_right so a point becomes active exactly at its timestamp. Before the first point return its first value; after the last return its last value. Step mode holds the current value. Linear mode uses the surrounding points and the fraction (elapsed-start)/(end-start); parsers ensure finite numerical values and strictly increasing times. Return a number, category or None without mutation. This low-level method assumes a validated track/time; Scenario sampling methods perform public time validation.

functions.name: _track
functions.description: Convert one battery constant or timeline into an immutable Track. Signal identifies engineering units/range through SIGNALS. A scalar becomes a single step point at t=0 seconds. A dict permits only interpolation and points, with step default or linear; each nonempty point must have finite, nonnegative, strictly increasing t and an in-range value. Return a tuple-backed Track. Invalid shape, mode, timestamp or engineering value raises ValueError; no I/O.

functions.name: _auxiliary_value
functions.description: Validate one synthetic screen input without assigning vehicle wire semantics. Speed uses km/h and accepts finite 0..65535 or None. Drive mode accepts N/D/R or None. Each named status accepts unknown/ok/fault. Return the validated number, string or None; reject booleans, unsupported types/values and unknown names with ValueError. These values are host UI inputs, not decoded physical CAN signals.

functions.name: _auxiliary_track
functions.description: Parse one synthetic speed, mode or status track with explicit unknown values. Constants become a t=0 step Track. Timeline dicts permit interpolation/points only and require nonempty, complete, ordered points with t in seconds. Each point must include value even when it is None. Linear interpolation is allowed only for numerical speed points; mode, status and null speed use step changes. Return an immutable Track; malformed shapes/times/values raise ValueError.

functions.name: _auxiliary_tracks
functions.description: Build the complete synthetic auxiliary input mapping. Input object permits speed_kph, drive_mode and statuses; statuses permits the seven AUXILIARY_STATUS_NAMES. Omitted speed/mode become None and omitted statuses become unknown. Return nine newly parsed Tracks, validating every supplied value and rejecting unknown keys with ValueError. No battery values are derived from these inputs and no vehicle CAN identifiers/polarities are allocated.

functions.name: _auxiliary_wired
functions.description: Name the auxiliary inputs a scenario explicitly provides. Input is the already-validated auxiliary object. Return speed_kph/drive_mode when their keys are present and every named status, including ones whose value is "unknown" or null: a provided input is wired, so its missing data is a malfunction. Omitted inputs are unwired, like production firmware, and are never written to the fault history.

functions.name: _unknown_auxiliary_tracks
functions.description: Allocate the default auxiliary tracks for direct Scenario construction. Called as the dataclass default_factory with no arguments. Return fresh unknown speed/mode/status tracks via the same parser used for JSON inputs, so separate Scenario instances do not share a mutable default dict. Existing three-argument Scenario(duration, tracks, faults) callers retain explicit auxiliary unknowns.

functions.name: _fault
functions.description: Validate and normalize one timed CAN response fault. Index is the stable JSON-list position used for drop counters. Require a known type and interval 0 <= start < end in seconds; optional signal must name a battery PID. Accept only this type's parameter keys, fill type defaults, then validate seconds/spacing and bounded integer parameters. unknown_pid must be absent from the firmware table; raw requires a target and a width-fitting value. Return Fault(index, interval, type, target, parameters); invalid inputs raise ValueError. Interval activation itself is handled by Scenario.active_faults.

functions.name: Scenario.from_dict
functions.description: Parse the version-one scenario schema into battery, auxiliary and fault tracks. Input is a JSON-like object with version/duration/signals/faults/auxiliary only. Default version is 1, duration is 10 seconds, omitted battery signals are synthetic engineering zero, and omitted auxiliary inputs are unknown. Require positive finite duration and a fault list. Enumerate faults in configuration order for stable counter identity, then return a new Scenario. Validation raises ValueError before any bus, C host or output artifact is opened.

functions.name: Scenario.from_text
functions.description: Decode a captured JSON string and validate the complete scenario. Input text is the exact configuration contents, not a path. json.loads calls _unique_object for each JSON object, making duplicate fields fail before from_dict builds tracks. Return a new Scenario; malformed JSON raises the JSON parser's error and unsupported schema/value data raises ValueError. No file I/O.

functions.name: Scenario.from_file
functions.description: Read a user-editable UTF-8 JSON scenario from a string or Path. Read the whole file once and pass its text through duplicate-aware JSON parsing and schema validation. Return Scenario; propagate filesystem/Unicode errors and validation/JSON errors. This only reads configuration and never opens CAN or changes the source file.

functions.name: Scenario.values_at
functions.description: Sample every configured battery track at simulation seconds. Require elapsed to be a finite nonnegative JSON number, rejecting bool/string and invalid times with ValueError. Return a new name-to-float dict in SIGNALS engineering units using each Track's endpoint/step/linear behavior. No transport, logging or track mutation occurs; omitted configured signals remain synthetic zero.

functions.name: Scenario.auxiliary_at
functions.description: Sample synthetic screen inputs at a finite nonnegative time in seconds. Validate elapsed before looking up tracks. Return a fresh dict with speed_kph, drive_mode and a new statuses dict for all seven names. Values preserve None and unknown explicitly; speed is still numerical km/h here and host conversion rounds later. Invalid time raises ValueError. Changing the returned mapping does not change tracks, and this method performs no CAN or electrical interpretation.

functions.name: Scenario.active_faults
functions.description: Select configured faults applying to one signal at a supplied time. Elapsed uses simulation seconds and signal is the request's battery name. Return a tuple in original configuration order when start <= elapsed < end and target is either None (all signals) or the requested name. No counters advance here; Responder.plan counts matching drop requests. This selector assumes the caller already validated elapsed/name and performs no I/O or mutation.

functions.name: validate_vcan
functions.description: Verify that a requested SocketCAN interface is a Linux software vcan device. Channel must match vcan followed by digits. platform/sysfs_root can be injected by tests; production defaults use this OS and /sys. Require the class/net symlink to resolve to devices/virtual/net/channel, ARPHRD_CAN type text 280 and no device node. Then run ip -details -json link show dev with a five-second timeout and require exactly one matching interface with info_kind vcan. Return None on success. Failures raise ValueError, including missing/malformed kernel evidence. This reads metadata and runs ip; it never creates an interface or sends a frame.

functions.name: open_bus
functions.description: Open one supported simulation endpoint while ignoring external CAN configuration. Channel is a nonempty string of at most 128 characters. virtual creates a same-process python-can endpoint with a 1024-frame receive queue and no own-message reception. socketcan first verifies Linux vcan, then opens that software endpoint. Return BusABC; caller must close/shutdown it. Unsupported backend/channel metadata raises ValueError and bus-open errors propagate. Physical adapters cannot be selected through this function; environment/user CAN settings are ignored.

functions.name: dashboard_host_set_tick
functions.description: Set the clock read by the unchanged production scheduler. Input: tick is an absolute unsigned millisecond value chosen by the command runner. Returns nothing; replaces host_tick only. The fake imposes no monotonic rule; the T command parser enforces it before calling.

functions.name: HAL_GetTick
functions.description: Read simulated time without waiting. Inputs: none. Returns host_tick in milliseconds with no mutation or sleep; production request-period/timeout arithmetic reads this value.

functions.name: host_dlc
functions.description: Convert a canonical byte length to the vendor HAL's DLC encoding. Input: size is a payload byte count. Returns the index of the 16 canonical HAL DLC sizes (0..8,12,16,20,24,32,48,64), or -1. No frame or queue state changes.

functions.name: dashboard_host_receive
functions.description: Add one frame to the finite receive batch, retaining metadata for decoder rejection tests. Inputs: id and metadata describe a synthetic frame; data contains size bytes and can be null only for size zero. Returns false for unsupported lengths, full 128-entry batch or absent payload; otherwise copies bytes/metadata into the next RX slot. Rejection by the production protocol decoder happens later.

functions.name: HAL_FDCAN_GetTxFifoFreeLevel
functions.description: Model one available transmit slot, without bitrate or arbitration simulation. Input: handle is deliberately ignored. Returns one available slot unconditionally; actual pending-request rejection occurs in AddMessageToTxFifoQ. The fake does not reproduce a hardware FIFO fill level.

functions.name: HAL_FDCAN_AddMessageToTxFifoQ
functions.description: Capture the actual request generated by production C. Inputs: header and data are valid production request buffers; handle is ignored. Returns HAL_ERROR if the previous captured request was not consumed; otherwise copies header/eight bytes, sets tx_pending and returns HAL_OK. This function does not transmit externally.

functions.name: dashboard_host_take_tx
functions.description: Consume a captured request once. Input: tx is writable request storage. Returns false without consuming when tx is null or no request is pending. On true it copies outgoing then clears tx_pending, making the one-slot sink available for the next request.

functions.name: HAL_FDCAN_GetRxFifoFillLevel
functions.description: Expose the remaining receive batch. Inputs: handle/fifo are ignored. Returns queued-but-not-read entries as rx_write- rx_read; no hardware filtering or overflow interrupt behavior is emulated.

functions.name: HAL_FDCAN_GetRxMessage
functions.description: Copy the vendor DLC byte count into the production driver's receive buffer. Inputs: writable header/data buffers; handle/fifo ignored. Returns HAL_ERROR when empty, otherwise copies the header and full DLC-sized bytes (up to 64), consumes a slot and resets both indices only after the batch drains. The caller must provide 64-byte RX capacity; malformed protocol frames still reach production validation.

functions.name: HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig
functions.description: Accept synthetic clock setup without touching RCC registers. Input: clock is ignored rather than inspected. Returns HAL_OK always; no clock frequency/pin correctness is proven by this boundary.

functions.name: HAL_FDCAN_Init
functions.description: Accept controller setup in memory. Input: handle is ignored. Returns HAL_OK without controller state/register checks; this permits the actual production initialization sequence to run on the host.

functions.name: HAL_FDCAN_ConfigFilter
functions.description: Accept the driver's filter; metadata validation is still performed by production C. Inputs: handle/filter ignored. Returns HAL_OK; the host deliberately preserves malformed frames for software-decoder tests rather than applying the hardware acceptance mask.

functions.name: HAL_FDCAN_ConfigGlobalFilter
functions.description: Accept global filter setup without emulating hardware filtering. Inputs: controller and four standard/extended/remote policy values are ignored. Returns HAL_OK with no RX filtering side effect; verification of configuration values is covered by the separate CAN harness.

functions.name: HAL_FDCAN_Start
functions.description: Start a synthetic controller only. Input: handle ignored. Returns HAL_OK without enabling any controller/physical output; subsequent queue operations are ordinary memory accesses.

functions.name: HAL_GPIO_Init
functions.description: Ignore board GPIO initialization in host execution. Inputs: port/gpio ignored. Returns nothing and changes no pins/registers. CAN MSP calls execute but pin initialization cannot be verified through this stand-in.

functions.name: HAL_GPIO_DeInit
functions.description: Ignore board GPIO deinitialization in host execution. Inputs: port/pin ignored. Returns nothing and changes no registers or queue state.

functions.name: xSemaphoreCreateMutex
functions.description: Return a token for the single-thread mutex boundary. Inputs: none. Returns the nonnull storage-array address as a token; allocates nothing and establishes no exclusion. This is sufficient only for the sequential host runner.

functions.name: xSemaphoreTake
functions.description: Validate the token without waiting for another task. Inputs: mutex is a token and ticks is ignored. Returns nonzero exactly when the token is nonnull; never blocks or acquires scheduler state.

functions.name: xSemaphoreGive
functions.description: Release a token without scheduler effects. Input: mutex token. Returns nonzero for nonnull tokens; changes no lock/scheduling state because every host command executes sequentially.

functions.name: BSP_MMC_Init
functions.description: Initialize only the synthetic block array. Input: instance must be zero. Returns -1 for another instance, otherwise erases all 64 memory blocks to 0xFF and returns BSP_ERROR_NONE. Reinitialization discards host contents; it does not discover a real card.

functions.name: BSP_MMC_GetCardInfo
functions.description: Report a deliberately small host capacity covering the logger's fixed starting block. Inputs: instance zero and writable info. Returns -1 for a wrong instance/null pointer; on success writes total block count 4160 so production block 4096 has a 64-block region. This deliberately small test capacity is not board capacity.

functions.name: storage_range
functions.description: Check an address range before fake storage access. Inputs: block/count are 512-byte logical block indices/count. Returns true only for a positive range entirely in [4096,4160). Subtraction after the lower/upper guards avoids overflow from block+count; storage remains unchanged.

functions.name: BSP_MMC_ReadBlocks
functions.description: Read bounded fake blocks. Inputs: instance zero, writable bytes and bounded block/count. Returns -1 on invalid range/pointer/instance, otherwise copies count*512 bytes from storage and returns BSP_ERROR_NONE. There is no asynchronous DMA, cache maintenance or card-busy state.

functions.name: BSP_MMC_WriteBlocks
functions.description: Write bounded fake blocks. Inputs: instance zero, readable bytes and bounded block/count. Returns -1 on validation failure, otherwise replaces count*512 storage bytes and returns BSP_ERROR_NONE. Data persists only for this host process.

functions.name: dashboard_host_export_begin
functions.description: Clear the bounded binary-export sink. Inputs: none. Returns nothing; sets wire_size to zero before a dump so exports do not append to an earlier export. The underlying array is not erased because only the newly counted prefix is saved.

functions.name: HAL_UART_Transmit
functions.description: Capture binary export bytes, never a serial device. Inputs: bytes contains size bytes; uart and timeout are ignored. Returns HAL_ERROR when the 65536-byte memory sink lacks room, otherwise appends bytes, advances wire_size and returns HAL_OK. No serial device, wall-clock wait or partial write occurs.

functions.name: dashboard_host_export_save
functions.description: Write the captured binary stream to a caller-selected ordinary output file. Input: path names an ordinary output file. Returns false on open/short-write/close failure; writes the counted wire prefix in binary and closes even when fwrite is short. The memory sink is retained for inspection/reuse; no CAN/UART device is opened.

functions.name: BSP_MMC_GetCardState
functions.description: Host fake card writes complete synchronously.

functions.name: json_string
functions.description: Print a JSON string with control/quote escaping for real LVGL label values. Input: value is a valid terminated string. Returns nothing; writes quotes and escaped content to stdout without allocating. ASCII control bytes use JSON Unicode escapes; other bytes pass through, assuming generated label text is suitable for the JSON stream.

functions.name: json_label
functions.description: Print an existing label's actual text, or JSON null when no object exists. Input: label is a label handle or NULL. Returns nothing; writes actual current LVGL text rather than reconstructing a display value. The null branch writes a JSON literal and avoids querying an absent object.

functions.name: split_fields
functions.description: Split exactly count whitespace-delimited tokens; reject missing or surplus fields. Inputs: mutable line, writable fields array and required token count. Returns true only for exactly count tokens. strtok replaces delimiters with terminators and fields borrow storage from line, so callers must parse them before reusing that buffer.

functions.name: split_optional_field
functions.description: Split exactly minimum or minimum+1 fields; returns the number found, or zero when invalid.

functions.name: parse_integer
functions.description: Parse a complete bounded integer before narrowing; reject overflow and invalid syntax. Inputs: terminated text, base 10/16, inclusive int64-compatible bounds and writable output. Returns true and writes output only for a fully parsed in-range value; output is retained on failure. Initial digit checks, errno and end-pointer checks precede narrowing conversions.

functions.name: read_frame
functions.description: Read one bounded frame, rejecting invalid syntax, metadata and noncanonical DLC sizes. Input: input is the stdin-like stream, which must supply one newline-terminated record: hexadecimal id, three 0/1 metadata fields and payload hex or -. Returns true only after a canonical DLC payload has been enqueued. The 64-byte scratch bounds hex decoding; queue overflow, bad fields or truncated lines return false.

functions.name: print_step
functions.description: Emit decoded production values, captured requests, actual label/status state and log counters. Inputs: tick is simulated milliseconds, updated/logged describe this poll/append and data is the retained production snapshot in its named integer units. Returns nothing; consumes at most one pending production TX, queries real LVGL labels/styles and log counters, emits one flushed JSON line. All panel handles must have been created before calling.

functions.name: main
functions.description: Execute validated step/capture/export commands, retaining production singleton state between steps. Inputs: stdin commands T tick speed mode valid_mask fault_mask rx_count [wired_mask], following frame records, I x y pressed, S screen, H path, P path, E path or Q. Negative speed/mode mean unknown; speed is km/h, mode is 0=N/1=D/2=R and masks use seven status bits. wired_mask adds bit 7 for speed and bit 8 for mode; when omitted every auxiliary input is treated as wired (explicit host input). I sets the simulated touch point; the next T step lets LVGL read it. Returns 0 for orderly completion, 1 for initialization/read failure and 2 for malformed commands. T orders clock -> production CAN poll -> conditional RAM/eMMC logging -> battery/aux UI -> LVGL timers -> JSON. P refreshes/captures; E flushes and captures the logger binary stream to a file. State persists across T commands but this single-thread loop does not schedule FreeRTOS tasks.

functions.name: dashboard_render_flush
functions.description: Copy the LVGL area-sized pixel buffer into matching framebuffer coordinates, clipping any out-of-display coordinates while retaining the area's source stride. Complete the synchronous flush only after all included rows are copied. Inputs: driver is the display issuing flush; area has inclusive pixel bounds and colors has row stride equal to the original area width. Returns nothing; copies only visible destinations while retaining source indexing, then calls lv_disp_flush_ready. The copy is synchronous; no DMA completion is modeled.

functions.name: dashboard_touch_read
functions.description: Report the simulated touch state to LVGL; coordinates are display pixels. Inputs: LVGL driver and output record. Returns nothing; copies the last point set by dashboard_render_touch and its pressed/released state.

functions.name: dashboard_render_touch
functions.description: Press or release the simulated touch panel at a display pixel. LVGL reads it during the next dashboard_render_step at least LV_INDEV_DEF_READ_PERIOD ms later, then runs the same click and long-press handling as on the board.

functions.name: dashboard_render_init
functions.description: Register a partial-buffer memory display and create the existing main/debug screens. Repeated calls while active succeed without creating duplicate displays or objects. Inputs: none. Returns true for an already registered display or a newly registered one; false if registration fails. On first entry lv_init, buffers/tick reset, draw-buffer registration and ui_init precede the first refresh. The partial buffer is 480x32 pixels, while the retained framebuffer is 480x272.

functions.name: dashboard_render_step
functions.description: Advance the LVGL tick by the unsigned difference from the last simulated timestamp and process timers. The caller controls time; this function does not wait on a wall clock. Input: now_ms is absolute uint32 simulated time. Returns nothing; null display is a no- op. LVGL receives the unsigned elapsed difference, then timer handling runs; monotonic time (or intentional rollover) is the caller's responsibility.

functions.name: dashboard_render_capture
functions.description: Refresh the current display and serialize each framebuffer RGB565 color through LVGL's own color conversion to RGB bytes. Return false for invalid paths or file errors. Input: ppm_path is an ordinary output path. Returns false before refresh for a missing display/null path, or on open/header/row/close failure. On success produces P6 header plus 480*272*3 RGB bytes, using lv_color_to32 from the configured RGB565 colors. It does not reinterpret CAN values or synthesize browser graphics.

functions.name: dashboard_render_shutdown
functions.description: Tear down generated UI objects and remove the memory display and its remaining screen trees. LVGL's custom-allocation configuration keeps its global core initialized. Inputs: none. Returns nothing; null display is a no-op. Generated main/debug deletion, separate initial-actions deletion and display removal precede clearing the registered display handle. Shared global LVGL memory/core initialization is retained; no board peripherals are touched.

functions.name: run_live
functions.description: Serve the running dashboard on 127.0.0.1:port until interrupted; return 0. Build the sanitizer host, start real-time stepping and print the page URL. Ctrl+C stops the server, then the host (its exit status is checked) and the virtual buses.

functions.name: main
functions.description: Run a JSON scenario into local captures/logs and optionally open its player. Parse argv for scenario/output, optional seconds override, step milliseconds, capture interval (100 ms default, 0 off) and explicit --open. Read exact scenario bytes once, validate their UTF-8 JSON, build the sanitizer host and run the closed virtual loop with the source protected from output overwrite. Save those same bytes as scenario.json and print the returned summary. I/O/validation/runtime errors exit through argparse with status 1. On success return 0. Only --open calls the OS default-browser launcher for the completed index.html file URI; a false result or browser/OSError prints its saved path while retaining a successful run. No editing occurs inside playback; changed input JSON requires rerunning this entry point.

functions.name: createPlayback
functions.description: Create a timestamp-based playback clock with injectable browser timing for deterministic tests. Inputs: captures is an ordered array with tick_ms timestamps; environment provides now/requestFrame/cancelFrame in the same millisecond time origin; optional onUpdate receives state snapshots. Returns control methods sharing closure state (position, playing, speed, loop and pending callback). Empty/single/zero-duration recordings remain stationary. Input ordering is established by the Python runner, not revalidated here. Initial publication happens before returning controls.

functions.name: createPlayback.frameIndex
functions.description: Find the final capture at or before the playhead without assuming regular capture spacing. Inputs: none; reads closure captures/position. Returns -1 for no captures, otherwise the floor index using an upper-midpoint binary search. It does not change playback state or interpolate an image; ordered timestamps are required.

functions.name: createPlayback.getState
functions.description: Return a copy of the playhead and control state for rendering or verification. Inputs: none. Returns a new object containing scenario milliseconds, selected capture index and current play/speed/loop flags. Nested capture state is not returned or mutated. Calling it does not advance the wall clock.

functions.name: createPlayback.publish
functions.description: Notify the renderer after a time or control change. Inputs: none. Returns undefined; synchronously calls onUpdate with a freshly computed state when supplied. Exceptions from the callback propagate rather than being hidden; publication itself does not schedule animation.

functions.name: createPlayback.cancelAnimation
functions.description: Cancel the next animation callback when playback stops. Inputs: none. Returns undefined; passes the nonnull pending identifier to the environment and clears it. Null identifiers skip cancellation, allowing repeated pause/destroy without a duplicate cancellation.

functions.name: createPlayback.advance
functions.description: Advance scenario time using elapsed clock milliseconds and the selected playback speed. Input: wall is milliseconds in the environment clock origin. Returns undefined; if active, applies max(0, wall-lastWall)*speed and updates lastWall. Nonlooping completion clamps at end, clears playing and cancels; looping overshoot wraps modulo recorded duration. Exact end remains visible until the next positive overshoot. It changes clock state without publishing or loading an image.

functions.name: createPlayback.animate
functions.description: Process one browser animation frame and request another while playback remains active. Input: wall is the animation callback timestamp. Returns undefined; clears the consumed callback ID, advances time, publishes controls/capture choice and schedules the next callback only if still playing. Cancellation/completion therefore leaves no new queued frame.

functions.name: createPlayback.play
functions.description: Start playback, restarting at the first capture after a nonlooping completion. Inputs: none. Returns undefined; active, short or nonpositive-duration recordings are guarded. At the end it resets to start; it then records the current wall origin, marks playing, publishes immediately and queues animation. A repeated play call does not create parallel callback chains.

functions.name: createPlayback.pause
functions.description: Preserve elapsed scenario time and stop requesting animation frames. Inputs: none. Returns undefined; accounts for wall time accrued since the last frame before clearing playing, cancelling any queued callback and publishing. It changes no captured pixels/state directly and remains usable as destroy.

functions.name: createPlayback.seek
functions.description: Move to a bounded scenario timestamp while preserving the current play or pause state. Input: milliseconds is a finite number in the recording time range. Nonfinite values are ignored; other values clamp to start/end. Returns undefined; resets the wall origin so the next frame does not add time from before the seek, then publishes while retaining playing.

functions.name: createPlayback.setSpeed
functions.description: Apply a supported speed after accounting for time elapsed under the previous speed. Input: value must exactly match 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 or 4. Returns undefined; unsupported values do nothing. Current elapsed time is charged at the old speed before setting/publishing the new multiplier, preserving continuity.

functions.name: createPlayback.setLoop
functions.description: Change loop behavior without discarding elapsed scenario time. Input: value is coerced to Boolean. Returns undefined; first advances using the old loop setting, then stores/publishes the new one. Enabling loop after already stopped completion does not itself restart playback.

functions.name: createPlayback.replay
functions.description: Return to the first capture and start the recording again. Inputs: none. Returns undefined; seek publishes the first position and resets its wall origin, then play starts if needed. An already-playing clock remains in its single callback chain rather than being duplicated.

functions.name: mountPlayback
functions.description: Bind recorded playback to browser controls and commit each image together with its own decoded state. Inputs: captures includes tick_ms/image/state, document supplies the viewer element IDs and window supplies browser timing/Image/matchMedia APIs. Returns the clock controller. Controls disable when motion is impossible, and reduced-motion preference only suppresses initial autoplay. It creates image candidates separately from the displayed node to prevent a partially loaded or obsolete capture replacing pixels/state.

functions.name: mountPlayback.requestCapture
functions.description: Load a candidate image and reject callbacks from captures superseded by a newer seek. Input: index is the selected capture index; negative or already requested indices are no-ops. Returns undefined; increments a request-version token and sets an Image source, starting asynchronous load. Existing image/state remain paired until success. Only the current version may change visible output, including after rapid seeks.

functions.name: mountPlayback.requestCapture.commitCapture
functions.description: Swap the already-loaded image and its matching state in one event callback. Inputs: load event arguments are unused; this closure retains item/index/version. Returns undefined; obsolete versions stop before any mutation. Success replaces the displayed DOM node with the loaded 480x272 candidate, then writes that same capture's JSON state/timestamp and clears errors. The playhead may advance independently while loading.

functions.name: mountPlayback.requestCapture.rejectCapture
functions.description: Expose a missing capture and clear the screen/state pair before stopping playback. Inputs: image-error event arguments are unused; this closure identifies the failed capture/version. Returns undefined; obsolete errors are ignored. The current failure first seeks to that capture and pauses, then hides the image, clears decoded state and prints its missing filename. Pinning time before pause prevents late wall time from scheduling another capture and hiding the error.

functions.name: mountPlayback.updateControls
functions.description: Update the timestamp controls while keeping displayed capture state tied to its loaded image. Input: state is a clock snapshot. Returns undefined; writes range/playhead/ARIA text/button/speed/loop state and requests its capture index. It does not write decoded capture JSON itself: commitCapture performs that write only once matching pixels are loaded.

functions.name: mountPlayback.changeScreen
functions.description: Switching screens reloads the same capture time in the newly selected view.

functions.name: mountPlayback.now
functions.description: Read the same monotonic time origin used by browser animation callbacks. Inputs: none. Returns performance.now() milliseconds; no wall-clock dates or scenario timestamps are read.

functions.name: mountPlayback.requestFrame
functions.description: Request a browser paint callback for the recording clock. Input: callback receives the browser animation timestamp. Returns its requestAnimationFrame cancellation ID; browser scheduling may be throttled, so elapsed time rather than callback count drives playback.

functions.name: mountPlayback.cancelFrame
functions.description: Cancel a pending browser paint callback. Input: identifier is the queued browser animation ID. Returns undefined; forwards cancellation without changing scenario data or image requests.

functions.name: mountPlayback.togglePlay
functions.description: Toggle playing and paused states from the primary button. Inputs: click event arguments unused. Returns undefined; queries playing at click time, then pauses with elapsed-time accounting or starts via the guarded play path.

functions.name: mountPlayback.replayRecording
functions.description: Restart from the beginning when the replay button is used. Inputs: click event arguments unused. Returns undefined; delegates to replay, preserving the selected speed/loop settings.

functions.name: mountPlayback.seekRecording
functions.description: Seek to the slider's millisecond timestamp without changing play/pause. Inputs: input event arguments unused; reads slider.value and converts its string to a number. Returns undefined; clock bounds/finite guard apply before publication and asynchronous capture selection.

functions.name: mountPlayback.changeSpeed
functions.description: Apply the selected playback speed. Inputs: change event arguments unused; reads the select string as Number. Returns undefined; setSpeed accepts only the five supported multipliers and accounts for time under the prior multiplier.

functions.name: mountPlayback.changeLoop
functions.description: Enable or disable repeating the recording at its end. Inputs: change event arguments unused; reads the checkbox Boolean. Returns undefined; setLoop owns elapsed-time accounting and publication. It does not regenerate captures.

functions.name: build_host
functions.description: Configure and incrementally build the production-code host executable. No arguments. Prefer cmake beside this Python executable, falling back to PATH; absence raises RuntimeError. Configure tools/dashboard_host into build/dashboard-host with sanitizers ON, then compile with eight jobs. Capture diagnostics and limit each subprocess to 180 seconds. Return the dashboard_host executable Path; nonzero commands raise RuntimeError and process errors/timeouts propagate. Build files are written, but no MCU is flashed and no bus is opened here.

functions.name: Host.__init__
functions.description: Start one persistent C host process and reserve its diagnostic stream. Executable is the compiled host Path. Open text stdin/stdout pipes and a temporary seekable stderr file, avoiding a full stderr pipe that could block sanitizer output. Store the process and error-file handles; return None. If Popen fails, close the error file and re-raise. Hardware peripherals are implemented by the host adapter.

functions.name: Host.__enter__
functions.description: Provide this already-started host to a with statement. No additional process or resource is allocated. Return self; paired __exit__ owns shutdown and error-file/pipe cleanup. The caller may issue commands while inside the context.

functions.name: Host.__exit__
functions.description: Stop the C process, release handles and report exit failure when appropriate. The context supplies an exception type/value/traceback or None. If C is still running, write/flush Q, then wait up to five seconds; broken pipe or timeout forces kill and wait. Close stdin/stdout and read/close the temporary error file. Return None so a prior exception propagates. Raise RuntimeError with diagnostics for a nonzero C exit only when the context was not already leaving through an exception.

functions.name: Host.command
functions.description: Send one complete stdin command and read its single JSON result. Command text may contain the T header and subsequent frame lines; append a final newline and flush before waiting. Require readable stdout within ten wall-clock seconds, killing the process on timeout. Parse one result line into its JSON value (typed here as dict). Closed pipes, EOF or malformed JSON raise RuntimeError; EOF diagnostics come from the stderr file. Process/pipe state changes, not physical hardware. Calls must be sequential because responses have no request identifiers.

functions.name: Host.step
functions.description: Serialize one simulation tick, auxiliary UI state and received CAN batch. Tick uses integer milliseconds. Convert speed km/h to nearest nonnegative integer via floor(x+0.5), or -1 for unknown; map mode None/N/D/R to -1/0/1/2. Status names use AUXILIARY_STATUS_NAMES bit order: known sets valid, fault sets fault. Reject more than 128 frames before sending. Build T tick speed mode valid fault count followed by each frame's hex ID, extended/remote/FD flags and hex payload ('-' for empty data). Return the C JSON snapshot from command. Scenario validation is expected before this boundary; C separately checks typed range/framing limits.

functions.name: Host.artifact
functions.description: Ask the C host to save one framebuffer capture or binary dump. Command is the host operation (P for PPM, E for eMMC stream), and path is resolved absolutely. Reject CR/LF in the path with ValueError so it cannot split stdin commands. Preserve ordinary spaces as part of the remainder of the command. Return None only when C replies with ok true; otherwise raise RuntimeError. This writes a local file through the host and performs no serial/device export.

functions.name: ppm_bytes_to_png
functions.description: Convert the actual LVGL host RGB pixels into lossless PNG bytes. data is a binary P6 PPM with newline-separated header, maximum 255, dimensions exactly 480x272 and exactly three bytes per pixel. Reject unexpected headers or length with ValueError. Prefix each scanline with PNG filter byte zero, zlib-compress the unchanged RGB rows and return signature plus IHDR/IDAT/IEND. No screenshot approximation, palette conversion or external image library is used.

functions.name: ppm_bytes_to_png.chunk
functions.description: Pack one PNG chunk with standards-format length and CRC fields. Kind is its four-byte chunk type and payload its raw content. Return big-endian 32-bit payload length, kind, payload and zlib CRC over kind+payload. This nested helper allocates bytes only and writes no files. The PNG checksum is distinct from the dashboard binary-export checksums.

functions.name: ppm_to_png
functions.description: Convert a host framebuffer PPM file into a lossless PNG file. Read source, convert with ppm_bytes_to_png (which validates the 480x272 P6 format and raises ValueError otherwise) and replace destination. Return None; filesystem errors propagate.

functions.name: write_viewer
functions.description: Write an offline HTML player containing this run's capture/state records. Output is an existing directory and captures contains tick_ms/image/state dicts. Read the checked-in HTML template and playback.js, inline the playback code first, then replace the first capture placeholder with JSON whose '<' characters are escaped to prevent a data string from closing a script element. Relative PNG names keep saved playback usable beside index.html without a server. Replace index.html; I/O errors propagate. This only packages recorded results and does not rerun CAN.

functions.name: run_scenario
functions.description: Drive production CAN, LVGL and loggers through deterministic synthetic ticks. Scenario contains validated engineering/auxiliary tracks. Output selects replaced artifact paths; executable is the host binary. Validate positive finite duration (seconds), integer step_ms 1..1000, nonnegative capture_every_ms (0 disables images), 32-bit rounded end tick and at most 100001 steps before opening the host. Include an irregular final tick. Capture eligible ticks at/after each requested interval and always the end; default interval is 100 ms. Reject protected input aliases, including existing hard links, against every planned artifact before writing. Open two unique same-process virtual CAN endpoints and one persistent C host. At each tick dispatch due replies, drain at most 128 frames, sample auxiliary state, then let C process frames/update UI/loggers/generate its real next request. Record returned C state plus exact auxiliary input in snapshots.jsonl. Send the C-generated request back over virtual CAN and plan its response at the same tick; client delivery to C occurs on a later tick. Reject updated-but-unlogged storage samples instead of claiming success when the 64-block fake region fills. Capture actual C/LVGL PPM pixels and lossless PNG at chosen ticks. Request the production binary export, close resources, decode header/records/footer and require both stored/dump CRC flags true. Write battery CSV, packaged playback and summary; return counts and paths. Auxiliary inputs remain in JSONL/viewer, not battery binary records. Filesystem/validation/process/queue/CAN errors propagate and a failed run may leave partial local artifacts; no hardware or FreeRTOS timing runs.

Attribute calls remain spelled expressions; this collector does not infer object types or execute decorators/functions. ast syntax errors propagate.
