functions.name: collect_python_functions.visit
functions.description: Append definitions while traversing lexical Python scopes under prefix. Class names and enclosing function names extend the prefix. For each function, collect calls from its statements, obtain its own docstring/preceding comments and append source metadata. Then visit its nested definitions separately. Mutates only the collector's local functions list; no project class/function is instantiated or invoked.

functions.name: collect_javascript_functions
functions.description: Inventory JavaScript declarations, methods, arrows and callbacks using actual syntax. source is UTF-8 bytes from a JS file or one executable HTML script; line_offset restores the original HTML location. Nested body calls belong only to the nested function. Names carry lexical scopes; unnamed callbacks use a location label rather than an invented callable symbol. Comments on enclosing declarations/statements can document arrows. No object-member target or callback execution is inferred. Syntax errors raise ValueError.

functions.name: collect_javascript_functions.adjacent_description
functions.description: Read adjacent comments, climbing only the arrow's enclosing declaration/statement. A containing function is a documentation boundary, so its description cannot silently describe an otherwise undocumented callback. A comment at the start of a callback body may supply that callback's own explanation when no statement comment exists.

functions.name: collect_javascript_functions.body_expressions
functions.description: Collect one function's call expressions/identifiers, excluding nested callable bodies. Member expressions are retained verbatim as unresolved targets. Plain identifiers are references only; their presence does not establish that a callback was executed.

functions.name: collect_html_functions
functions.description: Collect executable inline-script functions with source lines relative to the HTML file. This extractor handles the repository's static script elements. JSON/data script types and scripts with src attributes are not parsed as inline JavaScript. No remote script is fetched; template placeholders in application/json remain untouched and unexecuted.

functions.name: collect_other_functions
functions.description: Return documented shell/CMake/assembly definitions using narrow line-based patterns. source is text and file chooses the language. Shell recognizes name() {; CMake recognizes function(...); assembly recognizes labels only when a function type/size declaration exists, excluding declared objects and internal loop labels. Adjacent preceding comments supply text. These records contain no inferred calls. Pattern coverage is intentionally limited and does not preprocess assembly or parse a shell/CMake runtime. Source lines and language identify where to inspect the full body. Missing explanations are explicit rather than generated.

functions.name: resolve_edges
functions.description: Return sorted, unambiguous symbolic call/reference edges between inventory definitions. Match language and declared names; prefer file-local C symbols. JS resolution uses visible lexical scopes and retains dynamic members as unresolved expressions. Duplicate eligible symbols yield no edge. Production files cannot resolve to tests or desktop HAL substitutes; host/test files may resolve their appropriate local targets. The input dictionaries are not changed. A reference edge means a symbol occurs/passes in source, not that a callback executes. Cross-language startup/interrupt connections require the inspected architecture guide and are not manufactured from same-name matches.

functions.name: project_sources
functions.description: Return a sorted, deduplicated list of maintained source/script/template Paths under root. Scan application, headers, generated UI, tools, tests, CMake and editor scripts; include the explicit root exporter/build/LVGL-config/linker files. Recognized extensions include JS/HTML so browser functions are auditable. Skip Python caches, vendor Drivers/lvgl and local build outputs. This boundary is a documentation choice, not a claim dependencies contain no code.

functions.name: collect_inventory
functions.description: Read maintained sources beneath root and return definitions, resolved edges and header gaps. Choose the language parser from each path; HTML parses executable inline scripts only. Check a leading comment/docstring after an optional shebang for a purpose header. A header check verifies presence, while the human guide/review establishes explanatory quality. No firmware or synthetic scenario runs here. File/encoding/parser errors propagate rather than silently omitting a file. The resulting dictionaries feed all generated documentation; missing source comments remain visible and can fail the CLI's --check mode.

functions.name: write_outputs
functions.description: Create output and write the inventory's JSON, Markdown index, Mermaid graph and offline HTML. The inventory is already collected/resolved. Stable source IDs map to Mermaid nodes and file subgraphs; call and reference edges use distinct arrows. Markdown escapes table delimiters. The explorer template receives inert JSON with '<' escaped so source strings cannot close its data script tag. Only these generated files are replaced; project implementations and upstream sources are untouched. Filesystem/template errors propagate to the caller.

functions.name: main
functions.description: Parse documentation CLI options, collect source evidence, write artifacts and return a status. --root defaults to this repository; --output defaults to its docs folder. --check turns any missing function description or file-purpose header into exit code 1, while still producing the inspectable inventory. Without --check, gaps are printed but return code is zero. Print definition/edge counts and gap locations. Filesystem/parser failures propagate rather than being treated as successful coverage. The module entry point converts the result into SystemExit; this command does not compile, flash or execute inventoried application code.

functions.name: ui_comp_get_child
functions.description: Send the component-child lookup event to comp with child_idx and return the child pointer supplied by its callback; return NULL if no callback supplies one. Inputs: comp is an existing component and child_idx selects its registered child. Returns the synchronously filled child pointer or NULL if unhandled. This helper does not bound-check an index; factories define the valid indices and must register the custom event first.

functions.name: get_component_child_event_cb
functions.description: Use the event user-data child array and event-parameter index to fill the child lookup result; no bounds validation is performed. Input: e must carry the factory-allocated lv_obj_t* array as user data and a writable ui_comp_get_child_t as event parameter. Returns nothing; modifies only info->child. Index range and pointer validity are a registration/caller contract.

functions.name: del_component_child_event_cb
functions.description: Free the component child-pointer array stored in the deletion event user data. Input: e carries the factory-allocated child pointer array, not owned LVGL objects. Returns nothing; frees the array once on the delete event, while recursive LVGL object deletion owns the actual widgets.

functions.name: ui_comp_Label1_create_hook
functions.description: Empty generated extension hook called with the newly created label component; comp is unused and no state is changed. Input: comp would allow customization of the new label. Returns nothing. The intentionally empty body neither stores the handle nor allocates resources; its only role is the generated extension point.

functions.name: ui_Label1_create
functions.description: COMPONENT Label1 /** Create a styled LVGL label under comp_parent, allocate/register its child lookup and deletion callbacks, invoke the creation hook and return the label pointer. Input: comp_parent is the LVGL parent. Returns the created label, initialized to 20.20 and centered with content size. The one-entry heap array survives until the delete callback; creation assumes allocation succeeds and the custom event ID is already registered.

functions.name: ui_event_DebugScreen
functions.description: event funtions /** Handle the supplied LVGL event by loading the main screen with a 100 ms fade on a long press; ignore other event codes. Input: e is an LVGL event. Returns nothing; uses lazy main-screen construction and preserves debug during a 100 ms transition. Non-long-press events do not change screen selection.

functions.name: ui_DebugScreen_screen_init
functions.description: build funtions /** Allocate/style the debug-screen image and battery/log labels, initialize text values, register its event callback and store the object handles in globals. Inputs: none; LVGL/default display must exist. Returns nothing; creates the background image then twelve labels: cell voltage, temperature, power and storage/debug rows. Fixed generated positions are pixels relative to center. Measurement/storage formatting is supplied by app_ui_apply_dashboard_data, not by this object builder; no allocation/repeated-call guard exists.

functions.name: ui_DebugScreen_screen_destroy
functions.description: Delete the debug-screen tree if it exists and clear every associated global object pointer. Inputs: none. Returns nothing; deletes the parent tree before clearing screen, image and all twelve label handles. It does not remove the display or free unrelated main-screen objects, and repeated teardown skips the deletion.

functions.name: ui_clamp_slider_value
functions.description: Return value clamped to the main-screen display range 1 through 100. Input: value is an arbitrary signed display scalar, not a physical CAN frame. Returns a value in [1,100] with no side effects; even zero/negative measurements draw at the minimum position.

functions.name: ui_slider_value_to_y
functions.description: Map the clamped 1-through-100 display value linearly to the knob Y range -5 through -147 using integer arithmetic; return the coordinate. Input: value is a display scalar. Returns a signed pixel offset relative to the centered parent; larger values move upward. Clamping happens before multiplication/division, and integer division yields discrete pixel steps without floating point.

functions.name: ui_temp_power_slider_color
functions.description: Return green for a clamped value through 40, orange through 65 and red above 65 for temperature/power indicators. Input: value is a display scalar, clamped to [1,100]. Returns an RGB565 LVGL color without changing an object. The thresholds are presentation constants rather than a verified vehicle alarm policy.

functions.name: ui_batt_level_slider_color
functions.description: Return red for a clamped value through 40, orange through 65 and green above 65 for the battery-level indicator. Input: value is a display scalar, clamped to [1,100]. Returns an RGB565 color without mutation. The reversed low/red to high/green palette indicates displayed charge level, with no vehicle fault decoding.

functions.name: ui_set_slider_image_color
functions.description: Recolor the existing fill image with color at full opacity and leave knob recoloring transparent; ignore each null image independently. Inputs: fill and knob are image handles or NULL, color is already an LVGL color. Returns nothing; fill recoloring is fully opaque while knob source pixels retain their original colors. The two null guards are independent.

functions.name: ui_set_slider_state
functions.description: If knob exists, move it to the coordinate mapped from value and apply color to the indicator images; a null knob skips the whole update. Inputs: value is the normalized display scalar, color is the preselected LVGL color, and fill/knob are image handles. Returns nothing; a missing knob prevents both movement and recoloring, while a missing fill only skips the fill write.

functions.name: ui_set_speed_demo_value
functions.description: Replace the speed label with the supplied decimal demo value if the label exists. Input: value is a synthetic integer written as decimal text. Returns nothing; no speed unit conversion is performed and it does not update CAN or auxiliary state. A missing speed label leaves the UI untouched.

functions.name: ui_step_demo_slider_value
functions.description: Advance the caller value by direction times step, clamp at 1 or 100 and reverse direction at either endpoint; both pointers must be valid. Inputs: writable value/direction pointers hold persistent demo state and step is a signed arithmetic step. Returns nothing; overwrites both direction at endpoints and value each call. This function does not track time or read sensor data.

functions.name: ui_style_status_panel
functions.description: Apply the main-screen black fill, rounded corners and green two-pixel border to the supplied LVGL panel. Input: obj is an already-created panel. Returns nothing; initializes the default style only, leaving visibility and later red/gray/green state decisions to the application binding. It assumes a nonnull LVGL object.

functions.name: ui_set_batt_temp_slider_value
functions.description: Update the battery-temperature knob position and fill color from the display value, using temperature threshold colors and 1-through-100 clamping. Input: value is the displayed temperature scalar supplied by the application, not raw PID bytes. Returns nothing; delegates position/color changes to existing images. It does not retain a measurement or interpret sensor validity.

functions.name: ui_set_power_consumption_slider_value
functions.description: Update the power-consumption knob position and fill color from the display value, using temperature/power threshold colors and 1-through-100 clamping. Input: value is a 1-through-100 display scalar after clamping. Returns nothing; this UI function supplies no energy integration or physical-unit conversion. The PWR kWh caption is static text; current application input is documented separately.

functions.name: ui_set_batt_level_slider_value
functions.description: Update the battery-level knob position and fill color from the display value, using battery-level threshold colors and 1-through-100 clamping. Input: value is the displayed state-of-charge scalar. Returns nothing; updates images only, not the battery data structure or logger. The shared knob guard prevents access before creation/after teardown.

functions.name: ui_show_main_screen_slider_demo
functions.description: Apply fixed demonstration values to speed, temperature, power and battery level; no CAN data is read. Inputs: none. Returns nothing; writes a fixed initial visual example (120 speed, 80 temperature, 50 power, 90 battery level). This is an optional presentation helper and does not consume the host scenario.

functions.name: ui_step_main_screen_slider_demo
functions.description: At most once per 40 LVGL milliseconds, advance persistent synthetic speed/slider values within 1 through 100 and apply them to the main screen; no CAN data is read. Inputs: none; reads lv_tick_get milliseconds and static demo values/directions. Returns nothing; one update is made per eligible call rather than catching up missed intervals. Unsigned subtraction tolerates tick rollover; static demo state persists between calls and screen recreation.

functions.name: ui_event_MainScreen
functions.description: event funtions /** Handle the supplied LVGL event by loading the debug screen with a 100 ms fade on a long press; ignore other event codes. Input: e is the dispatched LVGL event. Returns nothing; navigation lazily creates debug when absent and preserves the main screen. Long-press detection is LVGL input behavior; the memory renderer has no physical touch input driver.

functions.name: ui_MainScreen_screen_init
functions.description: build funtions /** Allocate the main-screen object tree, style status panels, labels and battery indicator images, register its event callback and store object handles in globals. Inputs: none; requires initialized LVGL/display resources. Returns nothing; creates parent before children, publishes global handles, applies center-relative pixel offsets, fonts and image sources, then registers navigation. Default texts/styles are placeholders until app_ui_apply_* overwrites them. Repeated creation and allocation failures are not guarded here.

functions.name: ui_MainScreen_screen_destroy
functions.description: Delete the main-screen tree if it exists and clear every associated global object pointer. Inputs: none. Returns nothing; parent deletion precedes nulling all child handles because LVGL recursively owns the tree. It is safe when the top-level handle is already null; static demo counters are not reset.

functions.name: ui_Screen1_screen_init
functions.description: event funtions build funtions /** Create the legacy Screen1 object with its frame image and store handles in globals; this source is absent from the current ui/CMakeLists.txt target. Inputs: none; requires initialized LVGL. Returns nothing; creates a root screen with the legacy frame image and stores ui_Image1. Its duplicate image handle name makes this excluded source unsuitable for linking beside the active debug source without a separate change.

functions.name: ui_Screen1_screen_destroy
functions.description: Delete the legacy Screen1 tree if it exists and clear its screen/image pointers; this source is absent from the current UI build target. Inputs: none. Returns nothing; parent deletion owns the image lifetime, then both globals become NULL. A missing root skips deletion. Current production/host source lists do not call this legacy lifecycle.

functions.name: ui_init
functions.description: /////////////////// ANIMATIONS //////////////////// /////////////////// FUNCTIONS //////////////////// /////////////////// SCREENS //////////////////// /** Register the component-child event ID, optionally install the default LVGL theme, create main/debug screens and the initial-actions object, then load the main screen. Inputs: none; LVGL and a default display must already be initialized. Returns nothing; publishes newly allocated handles and loads main after both active trees exist. It has no repeated-call guard or explicit allocation-failure return, so the owner controls initialization order.

functions.name: ui_destroy
functions.description: Delete the main and debug screen trees through their destroy functions; the separate initial-actions object is not deleted here. Inputs: none. Returns nothing; each generated destroy routine recursively deletes its own tree and clears handles. The display owner separately deletes ui____initial_actions0 and removes the display; this function does not shut down the LVGL core.

functions.name: _ui_bar_set_property
functions.description: Set a bar value with or without animation according to id; unknown IDs are ignored and the body has no effect when LV_USE_BAR is disabled. Inputs: target is an existing bar; id selects an animated or immediate value write, val uses the bar's configured integer range. Returns nothing; LVGL applies its own range handling. No local null check is provided.

functions.name: _ui_basic_set_property
functions.description: Set the target object X/Y coordinate or width/height selected by id; unknown IDs are ignored. Inputs: target is an existing LVGL object, id selects a coordinate or dimension, val is the LVGL coordinate/size value. Returns nothing; changes geometry and leaves range/layout handling to LVGL. The caller must supply a valid object.

functions.name: _ui_dropdown_set_property
functions.description: Set the dropdown selected index for the supported id; other IDs or a disabled LV_USE_DROPDOWN feature have no effect. Inputs: target is an existing dropdown and val is the option index, not option text. Returns nothing; no event is sent by this wrapper and no local pointer/index validation is provided.

functions.name: _ui_image_set_property
functions.description: Set the image source to val for the supported property id; other IDs are ignored. Inputs: target is an existing image and val points to the image source accepted by LVGL. Returns nothing; the source must remain valid for image decoding and this wrapper does not manage its lifetime.

functions.name: _ui_label_set_property
functions.description: Copy val into the target label text for the supported property id; other IDs are ignored. Inputs: target is an existing label and val is a terminated text string. Returns nothing; LVGL owns the copied text. This wrapper performs no null checks or formatting.

functions.name: _ui_roller_set_property
functions.description: Set the roller selected index with or without animation according to id; other IDs or disabled LV_USE_ROLLER have no effect. Inputs: target is an existing roller, val is its selected option index, and id determines whether to animate selection. Returns nothing; unsupported IDs make no write, with no local pointer/index validation.

functions.name: _ui_slider_set_property
functions.description: Set the slider value with or without animation according to id; other IDs or disabled LV_USE_SLIDER have no effect. Inputs: target is an existing slider and val uses its configured integer range; id selects animated or immediate application. Returns nothing; this direct setter does not send an explicit value-changed event.

functions.name: _ui_screen_change
functions.description: Call target_init if the screen pointer is null, then load the target with the requested animation, speed and delay without auto-deleting the previous screen; pointers must be valid. Inputs: target points to a screen handle; target_init creates that screen when absent. spd and delay are milliseconds and fademode is an LVGL transition enum. Returns nothing; lazy creation precedes loading. No local allocation/initialization failure is reported.

functions.name: _ui_screen_delete
functions.description: Invoke the supplied screen-destroy callback if it is nonnull. Input: target is a destroy callback rather than an object pointer. Returns nothing and changes only the state changed by that callback; a null callback is a deliberate no-op.

functions.name: _ui_arc_increment
functions.description: Add val to the arc value through LVGL and emit LV_EVENT_VALUE_CHANGED. Inputs: target is an existing arc and val is a signed delta in the arc's value units. Returns nothing; value is written before sending the event, so callbacks observe the new LVGL-clamped value. No object-null guard is present.

functions.name: _ui_bar_increment
functions.description: Add val to the bar value using the requested animation mode; do nothing if LV_USE_BAR is disabled. Inputs: target is an existing bar, val is a signed delta and anm is the LVGL animation option. Returns nothing; reads the current value before writing the sum and sends no explicit value-changed event.

functions.name: _ui_slider_increment
functions.description: Add val to the slider value with the requested animation mode and emit LV_EVENT_VALUE_CHANGED; do nothing if LV_USE_SLIDER is disabled. Inputs: target is an existing slider, val is a signed delta and anm selects animation. Returns nothing; sends the value-changed event only after the write, allowing registered handlers to read the new value.

functions.name: _ui_keyboard_set_target
functions.description: Associate keyboard with textarea when both LVGL features are enabled; otherwise do nothing. Inputs: keyboard and textarea are existing widgets. Returns nothing; the association is stored by LVGL, whose object lifetimes the caller manages. Compile-time feature guards precede any widget access.

functions.name: _ui_flag_modify
functions.description: Toggle or add the requested object flag for the matching modifier value; every other modifier clears the flag. Inputs: target is an existing object, flag is its LVGL flag mask, and value is the generated add/remove/toggle selector. Returns nothing; toggle first reads the existing flag, while an unrecognized selector follows the clear branch.

functions.name: _ui_state_modify
functions.description: Toggle or add the requested object state for the matching modifier value; every other modifier clears the state. Inputs: target is an existing object, state is its LVGL state mask and value is the generated modifier selector. Returns nothing; the resulting state may change style resolution in LVGL. No local object validation is performed.

functions.name: _ui_textarea_move_cursor
functions.description: Move the textarea cursor in the direction selected by val and focus it; unsupported directions still focus it, and disabled LV_USE_TEXTAREA does nothing. Inputs: target is an existing textarea and val is a UI_MOVE_CURSOR_* constant. Returns nothing; focus is applied after cursor movement. The wrapper neither inserts text nor reports a cursor boundary.

functions.name: scr_unloaded_delete_cb
functions.description: Extract the screen-destroy callback from the LVGL event user data and invoke it if nonnull. Input: e is the unload event carrying a screen_destroy_cb_t in its user data. Returns nothing; ownership/validity of that callback comes from registration. The event itself must be valid; the extracted callback may be null.

functions.name: _ui_opacity_set
functions.description: Apply val as the target object style opacity using selector zero. Inputs: target is an existing object and val is the LVGL opacity value. Returns nothing; selector zero targets the default style state. No conversion, animation or local value validation occurs.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_free_user_data
functions.description: Release an animation user-data allocation and clear the animation user_data pointer. Input: a is a valid animation whose user_data was allocated for LVGL memory management. Returns nothing; freeing happens before clearing the pointer to avoid retaining a dangling reference. Shared/static user data must not be passed to this callback.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_set_x
functions.description: Animation callback: obtain the target from a->user_data and apply v as its X coordinate. Inputs: a is a valid animation with ui_anim_user_data_t in user_data and v is in horizontal LVGL coordinates. Returns nothing; changes the stored target directly. The animation setup must supply compatible objects and valid user data because this callback performs no null checks.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_set_y
functions.description: Animation callback: obtain the target from a->user_data and apply v as its Y coordinate. Inputs: a is a valid animation with ui_anim_user_data_t in user_data and v is in vertical LVGL coordinates. Returns nothing; changes the stored target directly. The animation setup must supply compatible objects and valid user data because this callback performs no null checks.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_set_width
functions.description: Animation callback: obtain the target from a->user_data and apply v as its width. Inputs: a is a valid animation with ui_anim_user_data_t in user_data and v is in LVGL width units. Returns nothing; changes the stored target directly. The animation setup must supply compatible objects and valid user data because this callback performs no null checks.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_set_height
functions.description: Animation callback: obtain the target from a->user_data and apply v as its height. Inputs: a is a valid animation with ui_anim_user_data_t in user_data and v is in LVGL height units. Returns nothing; changes the stored target directly. The animation setup must supply compatible objects and valid user data because this callback performs no null checks.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_set_opacity
functions.description: Animation callback: obtain the target from a->user_data and apply v as style opacity using selector zero. Inputs: a is a valid animation with ui_anim_user_data_t in user_data and v is in LVGL opacity units (0 transparent, 255 opaque). Returns nothing; changes the stored target directly. The animation setup must supply compatible objects and valid user data because this callback performs no null checks.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_set_image_zoom
functions.description: Animation callback: obtain the image target from a->user_data and apply v as the LVGL zoom factor. Inputs: a is a valid animation with ui_anim_user_data_t in user_data and v is in LVGL zoom units (256 is unscaled). Returns nothing; changes the stored target directly. The animation setup must supply compatible objects and valid user data because this callback performs no null checks.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_set_image_angle
functions.description: Animation callback: obtain the image target from a->user_data and apply v as its LVGL angle value. Inputs: a is a valid animation with ui_anim_user_data_t in user_data and v is in LVGL angle units (tenths of a degree). Returns nothing; changes the stored target directly. The animation setup must supply compatible objects and valid user data because this callback performs no null checks.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_set_image_frame
functions.description: Save v as the animation frame value, clamp the image lookup index into imgset and change the target image source; user data must contain a nonempty image set. Inputs: a->user_data must contain a valid target, imgset and positive imgset_size; v is the requested frame index. Returns nothing; the saved raw value preserves animation state while only the source lookup is clamped. An empty image set is not guarded.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_get_x
functions.description: Return the aligned X coordinate of the target stored in a->user_data. Input: a is a valid animation with a compatible target in ui_anim_user_data_t. Returns the current value in horizontal LVGL coordinates; this getter changes no target/user- data state and performs no local pointer validation. Input: a is a valid animation with a compatible target in ui_anim_user_data_t. Returns the current value in horizontal LVGL coordinates; this getter changes no target/user- data state and performs no local pointer validation. Input: a is a valid animation with a compatible target in ui_anim_user_data_t. Returns the current value in horizontal LVGL coordinates; this getter changes no target/user- data state and performs no local pointer validation.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_get_y
functions.description: Return the aligned Y coordinate of the target stored in a->user_data. Input: a is a valid animation with a compatible target in ui_anim_user_data_t. Returns the current value in vertical LVGL coordinates; this getter changes no target/user-data state and performs no local pointer validation.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_get_width
functions.description: Return the width of the target stored in a->user_data. Input: a is a valid animation with a compatible target in ui_anim_user_data_t. Returns the current value in LVGL width units; this getter changes no target/user-data state and performs no local pointer validation.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_get_height
functions.description: Return the height of the target stored in a->user_data. Input: a is a valid animation with a compatible target in ui_anim_user_data_t. Returns the current value in LVGL height units; this getter changes no target/user-data state and performs no local pointer validation.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_get_opacity
functions.description: Return style opacity for selector zero from the target stored in a->user_data. Input: a is a valid animation with a compatible target in ui_anim_user_data_t. Returns the current value in LVGL opacity units (0 transparent, 255 opaque); this getter changes no target/user-data state and performs no local pointer validation.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_get_image_zoom
functions.description: Return the LVGL zoom factor of the image target stored in a->user_data. Input: a is a valid animation with a compatible target in ui_anim_user_data_t. Returns the current value in LVGL zoom units (256 is unscaled); this getter changes no target/user-data state and performs no local pointer validation.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_get_image_angle
functions.description: Return the LVGL angle value of the image target stored in a->user_data. Input: a is a valid animation with a compatible target in ui_anim_user_data_t. Returns the current value in LVGL angle units (tenths of a degree); this getter changes no target/user-data state and performs no local pointer validation.

functions.name: _ui_anim_callback_get_image_frame
functions.description: Return the saved frame value from a->user_data, which may differ from the clamped image lookup index. Input: a->user_data is ui_anim_user_data_t. Returns its saved int32 frame value without consulting the current image source; no mutation or pointer validation occurs.

functions.name: _ui_arc_set_text_value
functions.description: Format the source arc value between prefix and postfix in a bounded temporary buffer and copy the result into the target label. Inputs: trg is a label, src is an arc, and prefix/postfix are terminated strings. Returns nothing; the 32-byte temporary buffer bounds formatting and LVGL copies its result before the stack buffer expires. Long text can be truncated.

functions.name: _ui_slider_set_text_value
functions.description: Format the source slider value between prefix/postfix and copy it into the target label; if sliders are disabled, display zero between those strings. Inputs: trg is a label, src is a slider when enabled, and prefix/postfix are terminated strings. Returns nothing; enabled formatting uses the bounded 32-byte stack buffer. The disabled-feature path writes a formatted zero without accessing src.

functions.name: _ui_checked_set_text_value
functions.description: Set the target label text to txt_on when the source has LV_STATE_CHECKED, otherwise use txt_off. Inputs: trg is a label, src is an existing state-bearing object, and txt_on/txt_off are terminated strings. Returns nothing; reads the checked flag without toggling it and delegates text copying to LVGL.

functions.name: _ui_spinbox_step
functions.description: Increment the spinbox once for positive val, otherwise decrement once, then emit LV_EVENT_VALUE_CHANGED; do nothing if LV_USE_SPINBOX is disabled. Inputs: target is an existing spinbox and val selects direction only: magnitudes are not used and zero means decrement. Returns nothing; the explicit event is sent after the single increment/decrement.

functions.name: _ui_switch_theme
functions.description: Call ui_theme_set with val only when UI_THEME_ACTIVE is defined; otherwise this helper has no effect. Input: val is forwarded unchanged as a theme selector. Returns nothing; theme implementation/validation are supplied outside this helper when the compile-time theme switch is enabled.
